title: Fairphone 6 Plus Drops to $552.49 with 12 Replaceable Parts in Black Friday Sale
content:
The Fairphone 6 Plus is a mid‑range Android phone that has been marketed as a modular, repair‑friendly device. It is currently available on Amazon for $552.49, a discount of $98 from its original $649.99 price, as part of the retailer’s Black Friday sale. The phone’s price drop is highlighted as a key selling point for buyers who value its repairable design.

The 6 Plus features 12 user‑replaceable parts, including the battery, screen, USB‑C port, and cameras. All of these components can be swapped out with the screwdriver that comes with the device. Replacement parts are priced affordably; for example, a new battery costs $39.99. The phone also comes with a five‑year warranty and is eligible for up to six Android OS upgrades, which supports long‑term use.

In terms of performance, the Fairphone 6 Plus is powered by a Snapdragon 7s Gen 4 processor that handles everyday tasks smoothly. Its cameras produce decent photos, though they do not match the quality of higher‑priced models. The phone offers a clean, bloatware‑free Android experience and does not include wireless charging.

Additional features include modular back panels that can be swapped for optional accessories such as a card holder or cross‑body strap. The device also includes a dedicated switch for launching customizable focus modes called Moments, a feature praised by reviewer Allison Johnson for simplifying the homescreen and limiting access to distracting apps.
summary: The Fairphone 6 Plus features 12 user‑replaceable parts and is now available on Amazon for $552.49, $98 off its original price, as part of the Black Friday sale. The phone also comes with a five‑year warranty and up to six Android OS upgrades.
author: The Verge

title: Iranian IRGC hacking unit Shahid Kaveh sabotages French supermarkets' freezers
content:
In October, hackers altered the temperature settings of refrigeration systems in hundreds of French supermarkets, causing the loss of food worth millions of euros. The attack, described as one of the most unusual cyber incidents, targeted commercial fridges and freezers on a scale not previously seen in Europe.

French intelligence agencies traced digital evidence that included Farsi language fragments and other clues, leading them to an elite unit of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. The unit identified in the investigation is Shahid Kaveh, a group already known to Western intelligence services. Named after Mahmoud Kaveh, an Iranian commander who died during the 1980s Iran‑Iraq war, Shahid Kaveh operates under the Revolutionary Guards’ Cyber Electronic Command, which oversees several hacking units.
summary: In October, hackers raised temperatures in refrigeration systems at hundreds of French supermarkets, destroying millions of euros of food. French intelligence traced Farsi clues to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps' Shahid Kaveh unit, an elite hacking group known to Western agencies.
author: Ars Technica

title: Army detonates 68 barrels of lead azide at Iowa Army Ammunition Plant
content:
The U.S. Army detonated 68 barrels containing 9,700 pounds of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa, on Wednesday at approximately 9 a.m. CT. The controlled explosion was conducted to prevent a spontaneous, unmitigated blast of the unstable compound. The detonation launched gray-white clouds over southeastern Iowa and involved two earth-covered containers that were exploded simultaneously.

Local residents within a five-mile radius of the facility were advised to evacuate, while those living farther away were instructed to shelter in place. These individuals were told to close windows and doors tightly, turn off fans, and set indoor air systems to recirculate. A local news outlet captured footage of the plume, and a journalist reporting from a safe distance described seeing and feeling the shockwave roll through a nearby crop field. He subsequently put on a mask for the remainder of his live broadcast.
summary: Army detonates 68 barrels of lead azide at Iowa Army Ammunition Plant.
author: Ars Technica

title: US jury convicts Huawei of trade secret theft and Iran sanctions evasion
content:
A U.S. jury on Tuesday found Huawei Technologies guilty of stealing trade secrets from U.S. technology firms and of evading sanctions imposed on Iran. The jury’s verdict, which follows charges that began in 2018, includes convictions for bank fraud, conspiracy to defraud the United States, money‑laundering conspiracy, and substantive violations of the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.  

The decision comes at a time when U.S.–China tensions are high, as President Donald Trump is preparing to raise tariffs on Chinese goods. The Department of Justice issued a press release praising the outcome, saying it is essential for safeguarding the U.S. financial system, the global telecommunications industry, and national security.
summary: A US jury found Huawei Technologies guilty of stealing trade secrets from US tech firms and violating sanctions on Iran. The conviction also includes bank fraud, conspiracy to defraud the US, money‑laundering conspiracy and violations of the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, which the Justice Department said protects the US financial system and national security.
author: Ars Technica

title: Ars Live recap: Drone strikes hit data centers in Middle East, Russia and Ukraine
content: Drone attacks on data centers. Amazon data centers came under military attack for the first time ever in the Middle East this year, and Russia and Ukraine exchanged an unprecedented flurry of drone strikes on each other’s data centers. To examine what such attacks on data centers mean for the future of cloud services that all modern societies depend upon, Ars hosted a live discussion. In a conversation with Ars Technica Tech Reporter Jeremy Hsu, Joseph Jarnecki at the Royal United Services Institute first talked about why public cloud data centers have increasingly become military targets during the 2026 Iran war and the ongoing full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine: We see an increasing acknowledgement and fact of dual use in particularly the public cloud, but also just across the board in private cloud data centers as well. The dual use that I refer to is the utilization of compute functions within these data centers—within cloud services—by militaries, for example, to run battlefield management systems, to do their HR, to do their resource management. Once a military uses a piece of civilian infrastructure, at least under international law or in terms of the principles of targeting that are taken forward by militaries, it can sometimes become a military object and is therefore of interest to an adversary, and there's an incentive to target it. Jarnecki also highlighted the fact that relatively cheap kamikaze drones can inflict disproportionate economic costs and create widespread cloud disruptions when striking data centers: Read full article Comments
summary: Drone attacks on data centers. Amazon data centers came under military attack for the first time ever in the Middle East this year, and Russia and Ukraine exchanged an unprecedented flurry of drone strikes on each other’s data centers.
author: Ars Technica

title: Etsy CEO Kruti Patel Goyal says AI policy update won't train models on sellers' artwork
content: After backlash from sellers frustrated by Etsy’s new AI policies, which appeared to allow the company to train AI on user artwork, Etsy has now clarified its stance. In a note published on Monday, CEO Kruti Patel Goyal discussed recent tweaks to the company's terms of service and admitted that her team "should’ve given you more context on what the updates meant for your creative content." “Our recent terms update was meant to reflect the evolving technologies we're using to build better tools and experiences for sellers and the Etsy community,” Goyal wrote this week. “It was not meant to enable us to train AI models for the purpose of creating copycats of your items. We do not and will not do that.” Read full article Comments
summary: Etsy CEO Kruti Patel Goyal says AI policy update won't train models on sellers' artwork.
author: Ars Technica

title: Ladybird browser releases first downloadable alpha for macOS and Linux
content:
After four years of development, the Ladybird project announced its first downloadable alpha on November 23. The release provides prebuilt packages for macOS and Linux, replacing the earlier requirement that users compile the browser from source. The new installer also supports automatic updating, making the software easier to obtain and maintain.

Ladybird distinguishes itself by using a rendering engine and the LibJS JavaScript engine that were written from the ground up, rather than being derived from existing browsers. Project lead Andreas Kling emphasized in the announcement that “the engine is our own, built from the ground up, and not a fork,” describing the surrounding browser as “modest, but functional.” 

A brief note in the release mentions that criticism has been directed at Kling’s public statements, and points readers to additional context in accounts by Kelson Vibber and Drew DeVault.
summary: The Ladybird project released its first downloadable alpha on November 23, offering prebuilt packages for macOS and Linux. The browser runs on a rendering engine and LibJS JavaScript engine that were written from scratch, not forked from existing browsers.
author: Ars Technica

title: FCC grants SpaceX conditional approval for up to 1 million Starmind satellites
content:
The Federal Communications Commission approved, on Wednesday, a conditional authorization for SpaceX to launch a constellation of up to one million Starmind satellites that are intended to function as orbital data centers. The commission noted that, if fully realized, the network would raise the total number of satellites in orbit by roughly fifty times the current count.

FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said the decision reflects a U.S. effort to ensure the technology creates opportunity, attracts investment and delivers lasting benefits, adding that it opens a new frontier for the computing infrastructure supporting America’s leadership and growth.
summary: In an extraordinary decision, the Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday granted SpaceX conditional authorization to deploy a constellation of up to 1 million Starmind satellites designed to serve as orbital data centers. If fully deployed, this constellation would increase the number of satellites in orbit by roughly 50-fold.
author: Ars Technica

title: Backblaze says upcoming privacy policy may allow selling customer data to advertisers
content:
Customers have voiced concerns after Backblaze announced a privacy‑policy change that will take effect next month. The updated policy indicates the backup and cloud‑storage provider may sell certain personal information to advertisers.

The company’s current policy already outlines that, in addition to data users voluntarily provide—such as an email address used to create an account—it automatically collects details including the software and operating system used to access the service, the user’s IP address, and the date and time of each request made to Backblaze.

The existing policy also states that Backblaze does not rent, trade, or share a user’s address or email address with any other company for marketing purposes without the user’s consent, and it does not specifically reference advertisers. No further details about the planned sharing were provided.
summary: Backblaze says upcoming privacy policy may allow selling customer data to advertisers.
author: Ars Technica

title: State AGs challenge Character. Ai plan to auction users' private chats
content: State attorneys general have challenged Character.AI’s proposal to auction off users’ private chats as part of a bankruptcy sale. The AGs say the sale would contain sensitive personal data from more than 21 million U.S. accounts, including 2.1 million accounts registered to minors.
summary: The proposed Character. Ai bankruptcy sale includes sensitive personal data from more than 21 million U.
author: TechCrunch

title: New York bans AI chatbot toys for five years over safety concerns
content: New York has imposed a five‑year ban on AI chatbot toys. The decision follows new research from Common Sense Media that identified safety failures, specifically exposure to inappropriate content and risks to children’s emotional development.
summary: New York has banned AI chatbot toys for five years. Research from Common Sense Media reveals safety failures, including exposure to inappropriate content and risks to emotional development.
author: TechCrunch

title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei calls rivals' AI control accusations absurd
content:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has dismissed rivals’ claims that he supports surrendering human agency to AI.  

He noted that leading AI firms are increasingly automating their own research and model development.
summary: Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, rejected accusations that he favors surrendering human agency to AI. He made the comment as leading AI companies are increasingly automating their research and model development.
author: TechCrunch

title: TikTok video shows two men left alone for Friendsgiving after guests cancel
content: A generation known for loneliness is putting their own spin on a millennial-made tradition that requires socializing It’s a TikTok scene straight out of a stress dream: two men stand in their freshly cleaned apartment, explaining how all but one of the people they invited to Friendsgiving flaked out at the last minute. There is a can of whipped cream on the table and a 6lb ham in the oven. According to the video, posted by pop-culture podcaster Jackson Strike, those who ditched were either tired, or sick, or had a difficult day at work. More than 1.5 million people liked the video and many flooded to the comments section to express their disappointment at what they saw as an epidemic of antisocial behavior. “Everyone wants a village until they have to be a villager,” one user wrote. “Time to get new friends,” quipped another.
summary: TikTok video shows two men left alone for Friendsgiving after guests cancel.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Life100 Instagram account offers advice on dealing with intrusive grandma questions
content:
Life100 has gained viral attention by showcasing the wisdom of two women in their 80s, offering viewers important life lessons. The series highlights a recurring scene: a grandmother confronts her granddaughter at the dinner table with invasive questions such as “Why are you still single?” and “When are you going to have kids?” The grandmother’s remarks are punctuated by unnerving thrusts of her steak knife, while the granddaughter appears uncomfortable but receives no acknowledgement from her grandmother.

Those who have experienced similar situations may recognize the pattern that follows. The granddaughter might attempt to deflect, potentially inviting more probing questions, or she may call out the grandmother’s rudeness, risking further escalation. The content underscores the tension and discomfort that can arise in such family dynamics.
summary: Life100, an Instagram account featuring the wisdom of two women in their 80s, has gone viral for sharing important life lessons. The account offers guidance for people dealing with grandmothers who ask invasive personal questions at the dinner table.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Aidan is one of thousands of students forced to verbally defend his honours thesis as universities take on AI
content:
Honours students are increasingly asked to sit oral assessments, and at the University of Sydney the practice has become mandatory for every student in the one‑year program.  

When Aidan Elwig Pollock enrolled, he did not anticipate that his 20,000‑word thesis would need a spoken component. The university now requires all honours students to defend their arguments in conversation with professors.  

The change follows the growing concern that AI tools can compromise the reliability of written research, prompting the university to demand that students demonstrate their work verbally.
summary: Aidan is one of thousands of students forced to verbally defend his honours thesis as universities take on AI.
author: Guardian Technology

title: EA Sports uses AI to recreate John Motson's voice for FC27 video game
content: Late broadcaster’s family allows EA Sports to create digital version of ‘Motty’ to commentate on popular FC27 First it was Val Kilmer, then Greta Garbo, but finally AI has resurrected a star the terraces can cheer for: John Motson, the BBC football pundit who died in February 2023, is coming back to commentate on the next generation of footballers – at least on a video game. The legendary commentator’s family has approved the use of AI technology to create a digital version of “Motty” – as he was ubiquitously known by generations of football fans – by EA Sports, which makes the popular football simulator FC27.
summary: John Motson, the BBC football pundit who died in February 2023, will have his voice recreated using AI for EA Sports' FC27. His family has approved the creation of a digital version of “Motty” to commentate in the game.
author: Guardian Technology

title: New York bans AI toys, including internet‑connected talking toys, for five years
content: The state attorney general says she would ‘not hesitate to enforce’ the five-year ban signed by Governor Kathy Hochul The New York governor, Kathy Hochul, signed legislation on Wednesday that places a five-year ban on the manufacture and sale of toys powered by AI chatbots, including talking stuffed animals, dolls and robots that use the internet to hold conversations with children. The recently re-elected governor, who has also placed a one-year moratorium AI datacenter construction in the state, said that parents shopping for children’s toys “should not have to worry that dangerous chatbots disguised as toys could expose their children to inappropriate conversations, manipulate their feelings or put their privacy at risk”.
summary: Governor Kathy Hochul signed legislation that bans the manufacture and sale of AI chatbot‑powered toys for five years. The ban covers talking stuffed animals, dolls and robots that use the internet to converse with children, and the state attorney general said she would enforce it.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Paris manifesto outlines approach to extreme wealth in AI era
content: It is possible for democracy to reverse the dynamic of oligarchy. But we must act now The explosion of extreme wealth in the world is the defining social fact of our times. When Forbes magazine began ranking the world’s largest fortunes in 1987, the wealth of the richest 0.0001% of our planet’s population equaled 3% of global GDP. Since that time, the wealth held by this tiny group of people – just 3,000 households – has ballooned and now reaches 17% of global GDP.
summary: Paris manifesto outlines approach to extreme wealth in AI era.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Amazon to launch Amazon Autos, selling Hyundai cars in UK in early 2027
content:
Amazon announced that it will begin selling cars in the United Kingdom in early 2027, launching a new Amazon Autos service. The initial offering will consist of vehicles from South Korean manufacturer Hyundai, marking the first time the U.S. retailer will sell cars outside its home market.  

The partnership is described as an effort to tap the roughly £200 billion British automotive market, and the move is said to have the potential to disrupt the existing vehicle‑retail landscape.
summary: Amazon plans to launch the Amazon Autos service in the UK in early 2027, offering cars from Hyundai. The move could disrupt the British vehicle retail market and will be the first time the US company sells cars outside its home country.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Haftar visits Ankara, meets Turkish ministers as Erdoğan readies first Libya trip in 15 years
content: Eastern Libya’s commander, Khalifa Haftar, travelled to Ankara with his son Saddam, where he met Turkey’s defence minister, foreign minister and intelligence chief. The meetings occurred as President Recep Erdoğan prepared his first trip to Libya in 15 years, and came days after Ukrainian naval drones sank the Russian warship Merkury at Benghazi’s naval base.
summary: Eastern Libya's commander Khalifa Haftar, accompanied by his son Saddam, met Turkey's defence minister, foreign minister and intelligence chief in Ankara. The talks came days after Ukrainian naval drones sank the Russian warship Merkury at Benghazi's naval base, while President Erdoğan prepares his first Libya visit in 15 years.
author: Euronews

title: Russian drone strikes kill seven in Ukraine, Kyiv drones hit three Russian refineries
content: Russian drone attacks killed seven people across six Ukrainian regions, damaging a Naftogaz gas production facility, a DTEK thermal power plant and power networks. Ukrainian drones struck Russian refineries in the Samara and Rostov regions and an airbase in Nizhny Novgorod, with Kyiv reporting hits on three refineries.
summary: Russian drone attacks killed seven people in six Ukrainian regions and damaged a Naftogaz gas production facility, a DTEK thermal power plant and power networks. Ukrainian drones struck refineries in the Samara and Rostov regions and an airbase in the Nizhny Novgorod region.
author: Euronews

title: US Army detonates about five tonnes of lead azide, destroying entire stockpile
content: A video captures a massive explosion as the U.S. Army detonates approximately five tonnes of degraded lead azide at an ammunition plant in Iowa. The blast eliminated the nation’s entire stockpile of the explosive.
summary: The US Army detonated around five tonnes of degraded lead azide at an ammunition plant in Iowa. The explosion destroyed the country's entire stockpile of the explosive.
author: Euronews

title: Karachi building under construction collapses, killing 1 and injuring 10
content: A multi‑storey building under construction collapsed in Karachi on Wednesday, 25 November 2026. The incident left at least one person dead and ten injured. Emergency teams are now searching the rubble for individuals feared missing.
summary: A multi‑storey building under construction collapsed in Karachi on Wednesday 25 November 2026, killing at least one person and injuring ten. Emergency teams are searching the rubble for people feared missing.
author: Euronews

title: 14,000 march in Athens protest rising living costs, 24‑hour strike disrupts transport
content: Around 14,000 people marched in Athens on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, as part of a nationwide demonstration against rising living costs and stagnant wages. The 24‑hour strike disrupted metro services, grounded flights and kept ferries in port, affecting transport across Greece.
summary: Thousands demonstrated across Greece on Wednesday 25 November 2026 during a 24‑hour strike against rising living costs and stagnant wages. The industrial action disrupted metro services, grounded flights and kept ferries in port.
author: Euronews

title: Russia reportedly prepares nuclear satellite launch, discussed on Europe Tonight
content: Euronews’ new evening programme Europe Tonight hosted former NATO spokesperson Jamie Shea, who addressed reports that Russia is preparing a nuclear satellite launch and considered how such a development could affect satellite systems and its wider implications for the world.
summary: Russia is reportedly preparing a nuclear satellite launch. Former NATO spokesperson Jamie Shea discussed possible effects on satellite systems on Euronews' show Europe Tonight.
author: Euronews

title: At least 30 dead after fuel truck overturns, ignites highway fire in Cairo district
content: At least 30 people were killed in a highway fire in a Cairo district after a fuel‑laden truck overturned on a busy road, igniting nearby vehicles. The incident prompted a major emergency response, and authorities warned that the death toll could rise.
summary: A fuel‑laden truck overturned on a busy highway in a Cairo district, setting vehicles ablaze. The blaze killed at least 30 people and authorities warned the death toll could rise.
author: Euronews

title: US unveils proposed tariffs on 14 economies, including EU and China
content: The United States announced on Wednesday that it is proposing tariffs on 14 economies, among them the European Union and China. The tariffs follow a months‑long investigation into alleged excess production and represent the latest step by President Donald Trump to reshape Washington’s trade relationships. Before they can take effect, the proposals must undergo a period of public comment. The measures target several of America’s largest trading partners, and France 24’s International Affairs Editor Kethevane Gorjestani provides further details.
summary: The United States, under President Donald Trump, unveiled proposed tariffs on 14 economies, including the European Union and China, after a months‑long probe into alleged excess production. The levies, aimed at some of America's largest trading partners, must undergo a public comment period before taking effect.
author: France 24

title: Nvidia shares drop nearly 6% after Jensen Huang's return rally fades
content: Nvidia’s stock rally triggered by Jensen Huang’s return as chief executive weakened on Tuesday, with the shares slipping nearly six percent after a surge of more than 30 percent the previous day. The decline was attributed to ongoing doubts about investigations involving Huang and uncertainty surrounding the broader AI investment boom. Huang had resigned on November 12 amid allegations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy. The market reaction reflects lingering concerns despite his comeback.
summary: A rally sparked by Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia's chief executive faded on Tuesday, with the company's shares falling as doubts persisted over the probes he faces and the fate of the AI investment boom. After vaulting more than 30 percent on Monday following Huang's shock comeback, Nvidia fell almost six percent Tuesday.
author: France 24

title: Spain's Supreme Court closes criminal case against Carles Puigdemont
content: Spain’s Supreme Court has closed criminal proceedings against former Catalan separatist leader Carles Puigdemont, applying the controversial amnesty law passed by parliament in 2024. The ruling addresses his role in the region’s failed 2017 independence bid and marks the final step in implementing the legislation. This decision arrives ahead of a snap general election scheduled for Sunday.
summary: Spain's Supreme Court applied a controversial amnesty law to former Catalan separatist leader Carles Puigdemont, closing criminal proceedings over his role in the failed 2017 independence bid. The decision, the final step in implementing the 2024 amnesty law, was issued ahead of a snap general election on Sunday.
author: France 24

title: Parlan, France doubles population with virtually free land offers
content:
France’s mayors convened in Paris for their annual convention, where the decline in living standards and public services across both urban and rural areas was a central topic. Rural leaders highlighted concerns about shrinking populations in their communities, emphasizing the need for strategies to reverse this trend.  

In contrast, the small town of Parlan in the Cantal region has seen its population double and local services flourish. The town’s growth is attributed to an initiative offering virtually free plots of land, which has attracted new residents and revitalized community life.
summary: Parlan, a small town in the Cantal region of France, has seen its population double. The growth is attributed to the town’s offer of virtually free plots of land, which has helped local services flourish.
author: France 24

title: Paris launches initiatives to counter masculinist movements
content: Paris is confronting masculinist movements as they face their first major trial in the city. Local authorities have announced several initiatives to counter the ideology, with a campaign designed to highlight the real‑world danger posed by misogynist groups online. FRANCE 24 correspondent Gabrielle Nadler reports on the developments.
summary: Paris announces initiatives to combat masculinist movements amid their first major trial. The campaign highlights the real‑world danger posed by misogynist groups online.
author: France 24

title: 19 killed in steel factory explosion in Aliaga, Turkey
content: An explosion at a steel factory in Aliaga, near Izmir, on November 9 killed 19 people. Observers note that the blast follows other incidents and underscores ongoing worker‑safety concerns in Turkey, while also condemning what they describe as repressive responses from both the government and the company.
summary: An explosion at a steel factory in Aliaga, near Izmir, on November 9 killed 19 people. Observers say the tragedy highlights worker‑safety issues and condemn repressive responses from the government and the company.
author: France 24

title: Cannes Mayor David Lisnard Reelected as Leader of France's Mayors, Eyes 2027 Run
content:
Cannes Mayor David Lisnard was re‑elected Wednesday as the leader of France’s mayors. The victory follows his recent bid for the Élysée, which he now seeks to build upon.

Lisnard’s Nouvelle Énergie movement is gaining momentum, positioning him as a potential reshaper of France’s right‑wing politics. The party’s direction remains under scrutiny as it moves toward the 2027 election.

Observers question whether Lisnard’s campaign will truly alter the French political landscape or if his party will ultimately align more closely with the far right in the lead‑up to the 2027 polls.
summary: David Lisnard, the mayor of Cannes, secured reelection as leader of France's mayors on Wednesday. He is pursuing a presidential bid with his Nouvelle Énergie movement, prompting speculation about reshaping the right wing or aligning with the far right ahead of the 2027 elections.
author: France 24

title: Fact check: AI deepfakes target Taiwan candidate Puma Shen, US abandonment claims spread
content: Ahead of local elections, Taiwan has experienced a rise in AI‑generated attacks targeting mayoral candidate Puma Shen. Concurrently, disinformation campaigns have circulated claims that the United States is abandoning the island.
summary: Ahead of Taiwan’s local elections, AI‑generated deepfakes have been used to attack mayoral candidate Puma Shen. Disinformation also circulates claims that the United States is abandoning Taiwan.
author: DW World

title: Indians continue to be drawn into Russia's war in Ukraine
content: Indians are still being drawn into Russia’s war in Ukraine, with the source suggesting that deception or desperation may be factors. The piece raises the question of what steps New Delhi could take to protect its citizens from ending up fighting in the conflict.
summary: Indians are still ending up in Russia's war on Ukraine, sometimes through deception or desperation. The piece questions what New Delhi can do to protect its citizens from fighting in Ukraine.
author: DW World

title: Peter Magyar meets Volodymyr Zelenskyy to reset Hungary-Ukraine ties
content: Peter Magyar, Hungary’s new prime minister, met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to discuss resetting bilateral relations. Both leaders said they aim to move beyond the “frosty and hostile” ties that characterized the period when Viktor Orban, described as Kremlin‑friendly, led Hungary.
summary: After years of frosty and hostile relations under Hungary's former prime minister Viktor Orban, his successor Peter Magyar is meeting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. They seek to reset their countries' ties.
author: DW World

title: UN aid chief Tom Fletcher calls for food, medicine access in war‑hit Yemen
content: UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher arrived in Yemen on Wednesday and warned that ongoing fighting is blocking families from obtaining essential food and medicine, especially in Taiz City. He called for greater access to war‑hit communities to deliver emergency aid.
summary: UN top aid official Tom Fletcher arrived in Yemen on Wednesday. He warned that the war is preventing families, particularly in Taiz City, from accessing the food and medicine they need to survive.
author: UN News

title: Somalia's Baidoa famine risk falls but millions still face severe food shortages
content: Global food‑security experts said on Wednesday that the risk of famine in Baidoa has lessened, yet millions of Somalis continue to endure severe food shortages and malnutrition across the country. The warning underscores that, despite the improvement in Baidoa, widespread hunger persists.
summary: Global food security experts warned on Wednesday that the risk of famine in Baidoa has decreased. Nevertheless, millions of people in Somalia still face severe food shortages and malnutrition.
author: UN News

title: David Pelicot joins fight against sexual violence, challenges men's silence
content: Two years after the Mazan rape trial, David Pelicot has decided to put his name to the fight against sexual violence – and to confront what he calls the silence of men.
summary: Two years after the Mazan rape trial, David Pelicot said he will put his name to the fight against sexual violence. He said he wants to confront what he calls the silence of men.
author: UN News

title: Gaza widows raise families alone, managing shelter, water and school from tents
content: For women in Gaza who lost their husbands in the war, providing for a family no longer means just putting food on the table. Now it also means finding shelter, hauling water and keeping children in school – all from a tent.
summary: Women in Gaza who lost their husbands in the war now provide for their families beyond just food. They must also find shelter, haul water and keep children in school while living in a tent.
author: UN News

title: Governments and experts meet at UN in Nairobi Nov 26‑27 on global housing crisis
content: Government representatives and housing experts will convene at the United Nations in Nairobi on 26‑27 November to discuss solutions to the deepening global housing crisis, which leaves billions without a proper place to live. The meeting aims to address how to improve safe, adequate housing worldwide.
summary: Government representatives and housing experts are gathering at the United Nations in Nairobi on 26‑27 November. They will discuss how to address the deepening global housing crisis affecting billions.
author: UN News

title: Liberal Senator Leah Blyth Defects to One Nation
content:
Federal Liberal senator Leah Blyth has announced that she is leaving the Liberal Party to join One Nation. The move was described by Nationals leader Matt Canavan as “disappointing on a number of levels”. In an interview with Radio National, Canavan said he had considered Blyth a friend and had received no warning before her decision.

Canavan added that he finds it disappointing when a senator elected on a party ticket changes parties after the election, noting that voters elect senators as representatives of a party rather than as individuals. He recalled Blyth’s prior support for net‑zero policies and her lack of opposition to recent hate‑speech legislation, which the Nationals had opposed.

Canavan concluded that he can no longer, in good conscience, claim the Liberal Party can “save this country”, emphasizing his belief that Australia is “worth fighting for” and that children should grow up proud of their nation with freedom and opportunity.
summary: Federal Liberal senator Leah Blyth announced she is leaving the Liberal Party to join One Nation. Nationals leader Matt Canavan said he was disappointed by her move, noting she was elected as a Liberal senator.
author: Guardian World

title: China misusing Interpol to target dissidents, says UK lawyer Ben Keith
content:
A leading British lawyer, Ben Keith, who specialises in Interpol “red notices”, says China is misusing the police‑cooperation system to target and silence dissidents. Keith told reporters he is handling five cases in which Chinese authorities have made what he described as questionable requests through Interpol.

The comments come as Hong Kong prepares to host Interpol’s general assembly for the first time, prompting concerns that Beijing’s use of red notices could affect the event. Keith’s statements highlight scrutiny of China’s requests for the location and detention of alleged suspects.
summary: A leading British lawyer says China is misusing Interpol to target and silence dissidents. Ben Keith, a specialist in Interpol red notices, said he is working on five cases involving questionable Chinese requests as Hong Kong prepares to host Interpol’s general assembly for the first time.
author: Guardian World

title: UK embassy warns of increased drink‑spiking and credit‑card fraud at Tokyo bars
content: Social media campaign fronted by British rapper Shao Dow advises tourists not to let their guard down The British embassy in Tokyo has launched a social media campaign warning visitors to exercise caution after a rise in cases of drink-spiking and credit card fraud against tourists in the Japanese capital. In a recent clip made in conjunction with the embassy, the British rapper and manga artist Shao Dow, a frequent visitor to Japan, notes that although the country “is incredibly safe, that doesn’t mean you can let your guard down”.
summary: The British embassy in Tokyo has launched a social media campaign warning visitors about a rise in drink‑spiking and credit‑card fraud targeting tourists in the city. The campaign features British rapper and manga artist Shao Dow, who advises tourists to stay vigilant despite Japan’s safety.
author: Guardian World

title: China flies first foreign astronaut, Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, to Tiangong
content: Muhammad Zeeshan Ali – the first Pakistani to reach orbit – greeted with Chinese ‘space handshake’ at Tiangong station China has flown the first foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station, starting what it says will be the globalisation of its space operations as the US-led International Space Station (ISS) enters its final years of operation. Floating through a hatch to enter Tiangong, Pakistan’s Muhammad Zeeshan Ali grinned broadly as he was embraced by the onboard crew in what China’s space agency called the country’s first foreign “space handshake”.
summary: China has flown the first foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station. The astronaut, Pakistan’s Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, the first Pakistani to reach orbit, was greeted with a Chinese ‘space handshake’ by the onboard crew.
author: Guardian World

title: Lululemon founder Chip Wilson says men may import Thai brides at Canadian women’s conference
content: Chip Wilson said men importing brides from Thailand was due to women waiting too long to have children The controversial founder of Lululemon suggested women in Canada are having too few children and this could lead some men to bring in brides from Thailand, in remarks that stunned attenders at a women’s leadership conference. Chip Wilson, who built the Vancouver yoga-wear startup into a global athleisure empire, was a featured speaker at the Leadership Forum in Calgary earlier this week, an event organized by Axis Connects to advance women in leadership. The organization says it aims to create space for “candid conversations about the barriers women face both in business and society”.
summary: Chip Wilson, the founder of Lululemon, was a featured speaker at the Leadership Forum in Calgary organized by Axis Connects. He said men importing brides from Thailand was due to women waiting too long to have children, remarks that stunned attenders.
author: Guardian World

title: Sri Lankan asylum seeker killed himself after being sent by UK to Eswatini
content:
Kishanth Peramalya, a Sri Lankan asylum seeker who had been convicted of sexual assault, was denied entry and transferred by the United Kingdom to Eswatini, a southern African nation with which he had no connections. After his arrival in Eswatini, Peramalya killed himself.

Peramalya had been among a group that set sail from India hoping to reach Canada and claim asylum. The boat was rescued by the Royal Navy in October 2021 when it encountered difficulty and was taken to Diego Garcia in the British Indian Ocean Territory, which hosts a U.S.–UK military base.
summary: Sri Lankan asylum seeker killed himself after being sent by UK to Eswatini.
author: Guardian World

title: Swiss tourist killed, British and American hikers injured by elephants in Cameroon
content:
A group of six hikers – four British, one Swiss and one American – was injured when they encountered a herd of about 15 elephants near the village of Bakingili in the southern part of Mount Cameroon National Park on 19 November. The tourists were on a path used by the elephants to reach a nearby lake and were accompanied by local guides.

One of the hikers, identified as Alain Throo, an insurance executive based in London, was gored and later died. The remaining British and American tourists sustained injuries.
summary: A Swiss tourist, Alain Throo, an insurance executive based in London, was gored and later died while hiking near Mount Cameroon national park. Four British and one American tourists were injured when their group of six encountered a herd of about 15 elephants on a path near the village of Bakingili on 19 November.
author: Guardian World

title: Way of the Warrior Kid review: Chris Pratt family film criticized as subtle as military recruitment
content:
A review of Way of the Warrior Kid describes the film as a cliché-ridden celebration of machismo and the military that is as subtle as a military recruitment video. The reviewer characterizes the Apple-produced film as a tone-deaf Karate Kid knock-off that greets the current climate with a shrug, noting its similarity to a MAGA-approved after-school special.

The critique highlights the film’s focus on a 13-year-old boy amidst reports that boys and young men in the US and UK are outpaced by girls on reading tests, face higher rates of behavioral difficulties, and encounter impossible body image standards from the manosphere. The reviewer suggests these societal issues should prompt careful consideration of such a film, but argues Way of the Warrior Kid fails to do so.
summary: The film is described as a cliche-ridden celebration of machismo and the military that centers on a 13-year-old boy. The review characterizes the movie as a tone-deaf Karate Kid knock-off that feels like a Maga-approved after-school special.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Caroline Shaw: Pulitzer-winning composer collaborates with classical and pop artists
content:
Caroline Shaw, the youngest ever winner of the Pulitzer Prize for Music, is currently performing with the Attacca Quartet at the Jahrhunderthalle in Bochum, Germany. The venue, located in an old steelworks, features defunct concrete cooling towers and massive exhaust pipes that Shaw noted with awe during a conversation on a concrete bench. Shaw, a Portland-based US composer, singer, producer, violinist, and viola player, is described as being in high demand.

Thirteen years after winning the Pulitzer for Partita for 8 Voices, Shaw has built a diverse career that includes collaborations with classical artists like Anne Sofie von Otter and pop stars such as Phoebe Bridgers. Partita for 8 Voices is characterized as an unaccompanied vocal work that blends speech, singing, baroque dances, and analogue versions of studio-mixed effects.
summary: Caroline Shaw is described as a Portland-based US composer, singer, and producer who has collaborated with classical giants and pop stars. She is the youngest ever winner of the Pulitzer prize for music, having won the award thirteen years ago for her work Partita for 8 Voices.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Rory Culkin discusses anxiety, fatherhood, and his famous brothers
content:
Rory Culkin, an actor known for his roles in Lords of Chaos, Scream 4, and Gabriel, recently shared insights into his personal life and career in an interview. The article explores his experiences with anxiety and fatherhood, as well as his relationship with his famous brothers. Culkin also discussed his collaboration with Stephen Graham on the film Nocturne.

During the interview, Culkin was photographed in a Manhattan park with his baby daughter, Havoc Moon. He explained that he suggested the first name, "Havoc," to his partner during a dinner when she was not responding to other options, while she chose the surname "Moon." Culkin noted that he saw graffiti reading "Havoc" on a nearby wall shortly after they returned home, which he interpreted as a sign from the gods to finalize the choice. He expressed hope that his daughter will be a sweet, quiet girl who plays the harp, contrasting with the intensity of her name.
summary: Rory Culkin shares how he manages anxiety and reflects on his life as a father to his daughter, Havoc Moon. The actor discusses his career and contrasts his Hollywood experience with that of his better-known brothers.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Blade Runner 2099 review: Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer star in TV adaptation
content:
The new television adaptation of the Blade Runner franchise, titled Blade Runner 2099, stars Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer as they track down a group of rogue replicants. Set fifty years after the events of the previous film, the series presents a neon-filled world where the replicants have won. In this future dystopia, the roles have reversed: “blade runners” are now replicants hunting down disobedient humans, and the capture and storage of human memories has become illegal. As humanity dies, these memories have turned into valuable contraband.

The review highlights the series’ visual style, describing every scene as packed with terrifying visual beauty and beautiful doomsday visions. It notes that the franchise has always been relevant to the age of AI, starting from the premise that enslaved robots have rebelled. The new version is described as acutely topical in an era where people are increasingly anxious about whether what they see or read is the work of machines.

The article connects the new series to the core themes of the original 1982 film by Ridley Scott and Denis Villeneuve’s 2017 sequel, Blade Runner 2049. It emphasizes that memory is central to the franchise, with the original film exploring how characters like Rachael (Sean Young) are devastated to learn their childhood memories are not real. Similarly, in Blade Runner 2049, K (Ryan Gosling) hopes his memories signify something close to human. The new television expansion continues this exploration of what it means to be human by focusing on the preservation of experiences as collections of short films inside the head.
summary: The new television adaptation features Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer tracking down rogue replicants in a neon-filled world. Set fifty years after the last movie, the story depicts replicants hunting disobedient humans in a society where human memories are illegal contraband.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Writer-director Beth de Araújo bases film Josephine on her childhood assault memory
content: Writer-director Beth de Araújo witnessed a brutal sexual assault as a child and has turned her experience into one of the year’s most powerful movies The film-maker Beth de Araújo likens the personal experience that inspired Josephine, her disquieting second feature, to a slow-acting poison. Early one Saturday morning when she was eight years old, Araújo and her father were playing soccer in Golden Gate Park, near their home in San Francisco, when they heard a woman scream. Her father, a former Olympic runner for Brazil, told her to stay and bolted to help; Araújo, scared and alone, ran after him, and instead found the woman in a clearing, naked from the waist down. Araújo was too young to understand what had happened, but she knew something was wrong. So, too, does an eight-year-old Josephine, played by the remarkable newcomer Mason Reeves, in the one scene crafted exactly to Araújo’s memory: Josephine, confused and restless, observes as the woman tucks her hands under her legs to keep them from shaking. She is further confused when her father, Damien, played by the aspirationally everyman actor Channing Tatum, seems extra keen to return to their soccer game afterwards, one of many echoes of Araújo’s memory in this taut drama. In real life, Araújo’s father “put on a face, put on energy and made it seem fun,” she recalled. “And I was like: ‘This is so weird. Why is my dad being so extra fun right now?’”
summary: Beth de Araújo witnessed a brutal sexual assault at age eight while playing soccer with her father in Golden Gate Park, San Francisco. She turned that memory into her second feature film Josephine, which depicts the incident with newcomer Mason Reeves as Josephine and Channing Tatum as her father Damien.
author: Guardian Culture

title: The Slightest Touch review: Colin Farrell and Emma Fogarty's marathon friendship
content:
Rachel Fleit’s documentary The Slightest Touch follows the friendship between Colin Farrell and Emma Fogarty, who met in 2010 while preparing for a Dublin marathon to raise awareness for Fogarty’s condition. The film captures their journey as an odd-couple story, highlighting the personal dynamics between the two as they navigate the challenges of the race. Although the documentary features carefully controlled and curated scenes to protect the privacy of both individuals, the result is described as an unexpectedly intimate and emotional piece of work.

Emma Fogarty, a resident of Abbeyleix in County Laois, suffers from epidermolysis bullosa (EB), a rare condition that causes permanent, agonizing skin pain and requires daily bandaging. Their connection began when Fogarty received an award at the People of the Year event in 2010 for her campaigning work to educate the public about the illness. At the same event, she struck up a friendship with Farrell, who is identified as a supporter and patron of the EB charity Debra Ireland. The documentary presents this relationship as a big-hearted narrative that is more complex than it initially appears.
summary: The documentary The Slightest Touch follows the friendship between Colin Farrell and Emma Fogarty, who met in 2010 while preparing for a Dublin race to raise awareness of her condition. Fogarty suffers from epidermolysis bullosa, a rare skin condition that causes permanent pain and requires daily bandaging.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Louisville coach Kelsey tells critics 'bring it' after Trimble-led win over No. 5 Texas Tech
content: Cardinals coach Pat Kelsey responded to critics of teams utilizing fifth-year players by stating, "Everybody can have their opinion. Bring it." This remark followed Seth Trimble’s performance leading Louisville to a 72-64 victory over No. 5 Texas Tech.
summary: Louisville coach Kelsey tells critics 'bring it' after Trimble-led win over No. 5 Texas Tech.
author: ESPN Headlines

title: LSU asks judge to dismiss SEC lawsuit over sovereign immunity
content: LSU is asking a federal judge to dismiss the SEC's lawsuit against the Tigers, arguing that many of the plaintiffs in the case are protected by sovereign immunity as state officials and that the league doesn't have jurisdiction.
summary: LSU is requesting a federal judge to dismiss the SEC's lawsuit against the Tigers. The university argues that the plaintiffs are protected by sovereign immunity and that the league lacks jurisdiction.
author: ESPN Headlines

title: Indiana drops to No. 14 as Texas and Tennessee overtake Alabama in CFP rankings
content: Defending champion Indiana dropped six spots to No. 14 in the latest College Football Playoff rankings released Tuesday night. Meanwhile, Alabama fell out of the top five after being surpassed by Texas and Tennessee.
summary: Defending champion Indiana fell six spots to No. 14 in the latest CFP rankings released Tuesday night. Alabama fell out of the top five after Texas and Tennessee moved ahead of the Crimson Tide.
author: ESPN Headlines

title: Steelers bench Aaron Rodgers to start Mason Rudolph against Broncos
content:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have benched four-time NFL MVP Aaron Rodgers, who will be inactive for Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos. The team announced that Mason Rudolph will start at quarterback. This decision comes after the Steelers lost two consecutive games, dropping their record to 6-4, and occurred just days before Rodgers turns 43.

Notably, head coach Mike McCarthy had publicly backed Rodgers only a day prior to the benching decision. The Steelers confirmed the move in a statement released late Tuesday night.
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers announced that four-time MVP Aaron Rodgers will be inactive for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos. Quarterback Mason Rudolph will start in Rodgers' place as the team sits at 6-4 following two straight losses.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Sandpapergate: Six burning questions remain unanswered in Australia ball tampering saga
content:
The Australian cricket ball tampering scandal, known as Sandpapergate, continues to generate controversy eight years after Cameron Bancroft was filmed holding sandpaper on a field in Cape Town. Although most individuals involved in the 2018 South Africa tour have publicly shared their accounts, not all details have been fully disclosed. The incident, described as a petty cricketing crime followed by a clumsy cover-up and a hurried investigation, resulted in penalties widely considered heavy for the main protagonists.

Despite the passage of time, the saga has become a persistent story within Australian cricket. As the scandal resurfaces with new and resurfaced allegations and counterclaims, the situation threatens to escalate into a civil war over the truth. The ongoing dispute highlights unresolved questions that keep the debate alive, challenging the finality of the original investigation and its outcomes.
summary: Most individuals involved in the 2018 South Africa tour have shared their accounts, but not every detail of the incident has been revealed. New and resurfaced allegations threaten to turn the fight for the truth into a civil war.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Cricket umpires discuss stress, social media, and technology in Wisden feature
content: Four umpires discuss how they deal with players, why they avoid social media, how technology is changing cricket and why umpiring beats being a football referee By Wisden Cricket Monthly Last summer, sat in a quiet ground at the fag-end of a four-dayer, with a few souls still kicking around and a clutch of cameras streaming what was left of the day live on YouTube, it struck me again what a great, strange sanctuary this place is, out there on the edges of the modern world. The game is trying to move, albeit at its own pace. Later that night, the day’s highlights would be landing on social media, available to all, for the game’s devotees to pore over and pick apart. More people are watching the County Championship than ever before. Streaming numbers show a growing audience in the UK and a widening uptake across the cricketing globe. The numbers aren’t yet earth-shattering, but how could they be, with such eccentric fare?
summary: Four cricket umpires discuss their methods for handling players, their avoidance of social media, and the impact of technology on the game. They also explain why they prefer umpiring cricket to refereeing football.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Ronaldinho returns to Serie C after 11-year career hiatus
content:
The Knowledge has published a new installment of its Q&A segment, featuring a question from George Jones about footballers who have experienced extended career breaks. Jones notes that Ronaldinho recently made his first professional appearance in over 11 years while playing for Ravenna in Serie C. The article poses the central inquiry of whether any other players have endured a hiatus comparable to or longer than the 11-year gap.

The source details the specific circumstances surrounding Ronaldinho’s return. His previous professional match was on 26 September 2015, when he played for Fluminense in a 2-0 home victory against Goiás, a game in which he was substituted after 45 minutes. The piece highlights a notable symmetry in his return: 11 years and 50 days later, he played for Ravenna in a 2-0 home win against Forlì, also being withdrawn after 45 minutes. The article also briefly mentions other topics covered in the issue, including the fastest team to progress from FA Cup winners to the first round and matches delayed by snowball fights.
summary: Ronaldinho made his first professional appearance in over 11 years for Ravenna in Serie C, marking a return since his last match for Fluminense in 2015. The Brazilian was withdrawn after 45 minutes in the 2-0 home win against Forlì, mirroring his previous final appearance.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Pelé and Maradona's first meeting arranged by reporter Guillermo Blanco in Rio, 1979
content:
A new book traces the early stages of the relationship between two of football’s greatest icons, beginning with a sunny afternoon in Rio de Janeiro in 1979. On that day, Pelé and Diego Maradona finally met after a series of aborted attempts to bring the two together.

Maradona had expressed to a journalist friend that his dream was to meet the Brazilian legend. The meetings were delayed for several weeks, largely because Maradona did not want to travel on a Monday—a day he had free to spend with his girlfriend, Claudia. After a few weeks of failed attempts, the meeting was arranged in Rio.

Reporter Guillermo Blanco, writing for the Argentine sports magazine El Gráfico, secured permission from Pelé’s representatives and was determined to make the encounter happen. He checked Maradona onto a flight on a Sunday night without telling him, collared the young player after the Argentine Juniors played Huracán, then hurried to the airport. Maradona boarded the plane with his father, his agent, and a photographer, marking the first face‑to‑face meeting between the two stars.
summary: Pelé and Diego Maradona first met in Rio in April 1979 after Maradona led Argentina’s under‑20 side to the World Youth Cup final. Reporter Guillermo Blanco organized the meeting, secretly boarding Maradona on a Sunday night flight with his father, agent and a photographer after Argentine Juniors played Huracán.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Usman Khawaja sends proposed joint statement to Cricket Australia CEO over sandpaper crisis
content:
Usman Khawaja has revealed that he sent a proposed joint statement to Cricket Australia CEO Todd Greenberg regarding the 2018 ball tampering incident in South Africa. Speaking on The Grade Cricketer podcast, the former Test opener outlined the text, which was intended for the entire 2018 Australian team to accept collective responsibility for the sandpaper crisis. Khawaja stated that the suggested wording has been put to Greenberg for consideration.

The proposed statement reads: “We accept knowledge as a team that we knew we were ball tampering by artificially altering the condition of the ball in South Africa in 2018.” Khawaja’s comments come amid calls for Cricket Australia to acknowledge that the team as a whole was aware of the ball tampering. Additionally, the former opener expressed disappointment regarding Pat Cummins’ recent press conference on the matter.
summary: Usman Khawaja proposed a joint statement for the 2018 Australia team to accept collective responsibility for ball tampering in South Africa. He has sent the wording to Todd Greenberg, Cricket Australia’s chief executive, for consideration.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Rangers win 3-2 over Aberdeen despite naivety and complacency, says McInnes
content: Rangers manager Derek McInnes admitted that his team’s naivety and complacency made their task harder, yet praised their resilience. The club secured a thrilling 3‑2 victory over Aberdeen, and McInnes highlighted the players’ ability to get the job done.
summary: Rangers manager Derek McInnes said the team's naivety and complacency made their task harder in a thrilling 3-2 win over Aberdeen. He praised the team's ability to get the job done.
author: BBC Sport

title: Newborn Hepatitis B Vaccination Rates Decline to 65.6% in 2026
content: A new study reports that the rate of newborns receiving the hepatitis B virus (HBV) vaccine dropped to 65.6 percent in 2026, down from approximately 80 percent between 2020 and 2022. The decline is attributed to parents rejecting the immunization, which was once considered routine, following confusion associated with RFK Jr.
summary: A new study reports that the rate of newborns receiving the hepatitis B vaccine fell to 65.6% in 2026, down from about 80% between 2020 and 2022. The decline reflects increased parental rejection of the vaccine, which was once considered routine.
author: The Hill

title: Democrat opens investigation into Venezuela oil deal with reported tie to Vance
content: Senator Maggie Hassan, Democrat from New Hampshire, has demanded answers after a report alleged that Vice President Vance had a connection to a major energy company that received a license to sell Venezuelan oil shortly after the U.S. captured the country’s president. Hassan, the incoming chair of the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, wrote a letter requesting information.
summary: Democrat opens investigation into Venezuela oil deal with reported tie to Vance.
author: The Hill

title: Scott Jennings urges Talarico, Colom to run for president
content: Political commentator Scott Jennings advised Democratic Senators-elect James Talarico of Texas and Scott Colom of Mississippi to run for president amid rising speculation about potential 2028 candidates. Jennings stated, “If I were Talarico or especially the guy in Mississippi, Colom … I would just go ahead and run for president,” offering his political consulting perspective on their prospects.
summary: Scott Jennings urges Talarico, Colom to run for president.
author: The Hill

title: Jim Cramer praises Nvidia CEO Huang's return after resignation amid affair reports
content: Jim Cramer reversed his earlier criticism of Jensen Huang when the former Nvidia chief was reinstated as CEO. Cramer, speaking on CNBC’s “Squawk on the Street” on Monday, noted that although Huang had resigned amid reports of extramarital affairs—including one with an alleged Chinese spy—he was now back in the role. “We may not like what he did, but he got off,” Cramer said.
summary: Jim Cramer praises Nvidia CEO Huang's return after resignation amid affair reports.
author: The Hill

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologizes to staff and says he attends daily therapy
content: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to the company during his first all‑hands meeting with employees since being reinstated, admitting he has been in therapy every day, according to new reports. He said, “I made some terrible mistakes,” and added that he was unfaithful to his wife and had hurt his kids.
summary: Jensen Huang, the chief executive of Nvidia, apologized to the company in his first all‑hands meeting with employees since being reinstated and said he is in therapy every day. He said he made terrible mistakes, including being unfaithful to his wife and hurting his kids.
author: The Hill

title: Sen. Van Hollen confirms Abrego Garcia self‑deported to Spain
content: Salvadoran migrant Kilmar Abrego Garcia, whose wrongful deportation sparked debate over President Trump’s immigration crackdown, self‑deported on Tuesday. Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D‑Md.) confirmed the move. ABC News reported that Abrego Garcia boarded a flight from a Washington, D.C.‑area airport to Madrid, Spain, as he faced deportation to one of several destinations.
summary: Salvadoran migrant Kilmar Abrego Garcia self‑deported to Madrid, Spain, after facing deportation. Senator Chris Van Hollen (D‑Md.) confirmed the departure, saying he would be safe.
author: The Hill

title: Trump to Meet Sen.-elect El‑Sayed About TrumpCare Rebranding
content: President Trump announced he will meet with Sen.-elect Abdul El‑Sayed (D‑Michigan) to discuss the rebranding of a single‑payer healthcare bill, formerly known as “Medicare for All,” as “TrumpCare.” In an interview with the New York Post, Trump praised El‑Sayed, calling him “very smart” and noting that the Michigan Democrat “did a good job.”
summary: Trump to Meet Sen.-elect El‑Sayed About TrumpCare Rebranding.
author: The Hill

title: Colom Says He’s Excited to Work with Trump at Itawamba County Town Hall
content:
Sen‑elect Scott Colom (D‑Miss.) hosted his first town hall in Fulton, Miss., after defeating incumbent Sen. Cindy Hyde‑Smith (R‑Miss.). The event, streamed by Tupelo‑based outlet WTVA, brought constituents and community leaders together to discuss local concerns.  

During the forum, Colom said he was “excited” to work with President Trump on several issues, including healthcare.
summary: Colom Says He’s Excited to Work with Trump at Itawamba County Town Hall.
author: The Hill

title: Man and Dog Escaped King Tide on Oregon Beach, Video Released
content:
Cannon Beach police posted a video showing a man walking his dog on the beach on Tuesday when a sudden surge of tide swept both of them toward the water. The footage captured the man narrowly escaping the current, and authorities reported that both he and his dog made it back to dry land without injury.

The police department noted that the man had previously received a citation for driving on another beach and had been warned to stay away from the ocean because a “king tide” was expected that day. The warning came after the tide’s unusually high rise threatened to engulf the shoreline.

“King tides” is not a scientific term; they are exceptionally high tides that typically occur during a new or full moon when the moon is at its perigee. The department’s statement added that rising sea levels, combined with El Niño and king tides, are putting the U.S. west coast at high risk of record flooding. The report cited California’s recent stress tests of low‑lying areas in San Francisco and the broader threat of high tides and floods expected over Thanksgiving.
summary: Cannon Beach police posted footage of a man and his dog being swept by a king tide on a beach, but both returned to dry land uninjured. The man had earlier been cited for driving on another beach and was warned to stay away from the ocean as a king tide was expected.
author: Guardian Environment

title: George Monbiot: No sustainable way to eat fish, slams Marine Conservation Society guide
content:
George Monbiot argues that fishing is as harmful to marine ecosystems as tobacco is to human health. He dismisses claims from conservation charities that certain fish are safe to eat, stating that those recommendations do little to protect marine wildlife. Monbiot calls the idea of a single “sustainable” fish choice a myth.

In April, the Marine Conservation Society released its Good Fish Guide, urging consumers to stop eating cod and instead choose hake. The guide presented hake as a more environmentally friendly option. Monbiot notes that the Society later acknowledged that hake had become overexploited due to increased fishing pressure.

Six months after the initial recommendation, the Society downgraded hake’s sustainability rating. The change was attributed to the species’ overexploitation. Monbiot questions how such a shift occurred, implying a lack of consistent or reliable guidance from conservation groups.
summary: George Monbiot argues there is no sustainable way to eat fish and criticizes advice from conservation charities. He points out that the Marine Conservation Society’s Good Fish Guide first urged eating hake instead of cod, then six months later downgraded hake as overexploited.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Iowa Army Ammunition Plant to Detonate Lead Azide Stockpile Amid Public Concern
content:
The US Army plans to detonate the nation’s entire stockpile of lead azide in Iowa on Wednesday morning. This controlled blast, scheduled for the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, follows multiple delays and an outpouring of public concern regarding potential health and environmental impacts. The facility is located in a small town in south-eastern Iowa with a population of approximately 400.

The operation aims to dispose of 9,700lb (4,400kg) of the bomb-making chemical. Authorities warn that the explosion risks releasing plumes of toxic chemicals within a 100-mile (160km) radius. The specific location where these toxins may land remains uncertain as it shifts according to changing weather forecasts.
summary: The US Army will detonate the entire 9,700‑lb stockpile of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown on Wednesday morning, after multiple delays. The controlled blast could release toxic chemical plumes within a 100‑mile radius, sparking public concern about health and environmental effects.
author: Guardian Environment

title: HIV Viral Control Needed, but Not Enough for Healthy Aging
content: A recent report notes that individuals with HIV display accelerated biological aging. Blood‑based biomarkers reveal functions resembling older individuals rather than peers of the same chronological age. The findings underscore that controlling viral replication is necessary but alone does not ensure healthy aging.
summary: HIV viral control is necessary but not sufficient for healthy aging. Individuals with HIV exhibit signs of faster biological aging than people without HIV, with blood biomarkers resembling those of older individuals.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Methylmercury impairs forebrain inhibitory circuits and causes abnormal behavior in mice
content:
Global efforts to curb mercury pollution have not eliminated the threat posed by methylmercury (MeHg). The compound continues to persist in the environment, bioaccumulating along aquatic food chains. Humans mainly encounter MeHg through contaminated seafood. The devastating neurological effects of MeHg poisoning were first highlighted by Minamata disease, officially recognized in Japan in 1956. 

Since that time, researchers have examined MeHg’s neurotoxic impact, noting sensory, motor, and psychiatric symptoms. Although clinical reports document behavioral disturbances in affected individuals, the specific neural circuits responsible for these abnormalities remain poorly understood.
summary: Methylmercury impairs forebrain inhibitory circuits and induces abnormal behavior in mice. Clinical reports show behavioral disturbances in people exposed to MeHg, but the neural circuits responsible remain poorly understood.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Doctor reflects on US losing measles elimination status
content: A doctor reflects on the United States losing measles elimination status, noting that for many physicians of his generation, measles was rarely—or never—saw in practice. That was a sign of how well vaccination and public health efforts had worked.
summary: The doctor says many physicians of his generation rarely saw measles in practice. He says this rarity indicated successful vaccination and public health efforts.
author: Medical Xpress

title: FDA approves first new hormone therapy for early-stage breast cancer in over 20 years
content: The FDA has approved a new hormone therapy for early‑stage breast cancer, the first such approval in more than two decades. This marks a significant shift in treatment for the most common form of the disease.
summary: The FDA has approved a new hormone therapy for early-stage breast cancer. This is the first such approval in more than two decades.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Long‑term rise in fasting blood sugar linked to poorer midlife cognition
content: New independent research published in the Journal of the American Heart Association finds that young adults with progressive rises in fasting blood sugar over multiple decades were more likely to have worse cognitive health by midlife. Participants who developed type 2 diabetes during the study also showed signs of structural brain changes.
summary: Young adults who experienced a progressive rise in fasting blood sugar over multiple decades were more likely to have worse cognitive health by midlife. The study, published in the Journal of the American Heart Association, also found that participants who developed type 2 diabetes had signs of structural brain changes.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Single Vaping Episode Impairs Vascular Function, Study Finds
content: Researchers find a single vaping episode impairs vascular function, even when vaping without nicotine. The study’s results will be presented next week at the annual meeting of the Radiological Society of North America.
summary: Researchers found that a single vaping episode can negatively affect vascular function, even without nicotine. The study results will be presented next week at the RSNA annual meeting.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Feng Jian's team discovers cytokinin–NIN module driving spontaneous root nodules in alfalfa
content: A research team led by Professor Feng Jian of the Institute of Genetics and Developmental Biology (IGDB) at the Chinese Academy of Sciences has identified a cytokinin–NODULE INCEPTION (NIN) regulatory module linked to spontaneous root nodule formation in alfalfa (Medicago sativa). This discovery explains how alfalfa can form nodules without rhizobia.
summary: Professor Feng Jian's research team at the Institute of Genetics and Developmental Biology (IGDB) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences uncovered a cytokinin–NODULE INCEPTION (NIN) regulatory module linked to spontaneous root nodule formation in alfalfa. title: Ultrathin 'rainbow' sails could power spacecraft and shade the Earth
content:
Ultrathin “rainbow” sails have been proposed as a way to power spacecraft and shade the Earth. The idea builds on the physics of solar sailing, a concept that uses the momentum carried by photons in sunlight to generate a gentle push when the light bounces off a surface.

Solar sailing has gained renewed attention over the past decade, with several proof‑of‑concept flights demonstrating that the force from photons is sufficient to propel a spacecraft. These demonstrations confirm that the technology is feasible and could enable new forms of propulsion and planetary protection.
summary: Solar sailing uses the momentum of photons to push on surfaces, enabling propulsion. Proof‑of‑concept flights in the last decade have shown that solar sailing is indeed feasible.

Atlantic activity was below normal, while Pacific activity was above average, including two disasters in Hawaii.

title: EU Law Volume Doubles to 47,600 Pages by 2025
content:
A new EU Bureaucracy Index has been released to measure the volume of EU law in force. According to the index, by the end of 2025 the EU’s regulations and directives totaled roughly 47,600 standard pages—an increase of 118 % compared with 2010. The data show that the body of EU law has more than doubled over the past 15 years and continued to expand in 2025.

The index identifies sanctions regulations and new sets of rules in environmental, consumer and health law as the main drivers of this growth. These areas have seen the most significant additions to the EU legal framework, contributing to the record‑high volume of binding legislation.
summary: The EU Bureaucracy Index shows EU regulations and directives in force reached about 47,600 standard pages by the end of 2025, an increase of 118% from 2010. The growth is driven mainly by sanctions regulations and new rules in environmental, consumer, and health law.

content: The early universe may have generated minuscule black holes that could still exist today. If present, these atom-sized objects might consume stars from the inside or trigger their complete explosion.

title: Claude AI and Levent Alpöge claim proof of Riemann hypothesis
content: Machines are bulldozing through hard problems to assert the power of their tech bro creators, not to advance human knowledge In most walks of life, trying something 12,363,153,437,138 times and getting the same result is reason enough to assume it works every time. Not in maths, where a conjecture that holds up more than 12tn times looks very probably true but doesn’t qualify as proven. That was the status of the Riemann hypothesis, one of the most famous mathematical conundrums in existence, until last week. Then Levent Alpöge, a mathematician working at Anthropic, said he and his collaborator, Claude AI, had crossed the line from conjecture to proof. Rafael Behr is a Guardian columnist
summary: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, announced that he and Claude AI had proved the Riemann hypothesis. The claim, reported by Guardian columnist Rafael Behr, marks a shift from conjecture to proof in mathematics.

title: Dolphins in large social groups live longer, Australian study finds
content:
Australian researchers have found that Indo‑Pacific bottlenose dolphins that maintain active social lives and large friendship groups tend to live longer. Decades of data collected at WA’s Shark Bay support the finding.

The study, published in PLOS Biology, notes that dolphins can live for more than 50 years and that group size increases during youth and early adulthood before declining toward the end of life. The research suggests that social engagement may influence longevity in these marine mammals.

Readers can sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s Clear Air column as a free newsletter.
summary: Decades of data from WA’s Shark Bay indicate that Indo‑Pacific bottlenose dolphins that socialise in large, consistently sized groups live longer. The PLOS Biology study found that group size increases during youth and early adulthood before declining toward the end of life, and that these dolphins can live more than 50 years.

title: Research shows tide height can differ by a metre across a beach, aiding local flood forecasts
content:
New research shows that tidal height can vary by as much as a metre across the length of a single beach. This variation is invisible when the sea appears level, but it has significant implications for flood predictions and for identifying locations most vulnerable to storm surges.

Until now, tidal information has come mainly from tide gauges, which record levels at a single point, and from satellite radar, which averages data over tens of kilometres. By analysing these differences in tidal height across beaches, scientists suggest that more localised tide and flood forecasts could be developed, improving accuracy for communities at risk.
summary: Researchers found that tidal height can vary by as much as a metre across the length of a single beach. The finding could enable more localized tide and flood forecasts, improving predictions of storm‑surge vulnerability compared with traditional tide gauges and satellite radar averages.
