title: Jensen Huang’s Return Shows Nvidia Is Too Big to Police
content: National security and foreign policy experts say Nvidia’s central role in the U.S. economy may have outweighed worries about CEO Jensen Huang’s ties to a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. The experts suggest that the company’s size and influence make it difficult to police.
summary: Nvidia's central role in the US economy may have outweighed concerns about its CEO's ties to a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. National security and foreign policy experts say the company's importance has made it too big to police.
author: Wired

title: Amazon offers Apple TV for $6.99/month, saving nearly $50 over six months
content:
Amazon is promoting a discounted subscription to Apple TV for U.S. customers who shop on its platform. The deal reduces the standard $14.99‑per‑month price to $6.99 per month for the first six months, amounting to $42 in total compared with the regular $90 cost for the same period. Amazon has not disclosed how long the promotion will remain available, and the source advises acting quickly.

The Apple TV subscription includes exclusive streaming of Formula 1 races and Major League Soccer matches, alongside a library of series such as Severance, Silo, The Morning Show, Pachinko, Pluribus, Slow Horses, and others. Recent additions feature movies from outside Apple’s studios, including titles like Arrival, Dead Poets Society, and Anchorman. While the service is described as ad‑free, Apple inserts skippable preroll ads that promote its own original programming.
summary: Streaming deals aren’t as plentiful as they used to be, but they’re still around if you know where to look. One that caught our eye is an offer for Apple TV for those with an Amazon account in the US.
author: The Verge

title: Sen. Mike Rounds proposes attaching FISA Section 702 to NDAA as deadline looms
content: Weeks before the end of the legislative session, some members of Congress are scrambling to reauthorize a controversial warrantless wiretapping authority, possibly by attaching it to a must-pass military spending bill. Sen. Mike Rounds (R-SD) told Politico that Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) could be attached to the National Defense Authorization Act. It's the latest in a grueling fight over a major spying rule that hasn't technically lapsed. "We don't have two weeks to work just on FISA," said Rounds, a member of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence. "But if it's amended onto the NDAA then you can mo …
summary: Some members of Congress are scrambling to reauthorize the controversial warrantless wiretapping authority known as Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act before the legislative session ends. Sen. Mike Rounds (R‑SD) said the provision could be attached to the National Defense Authorization Act.
author: The Verge

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang tells staff Trump's role in his rehiring is untrue
content:
Jensen Huang apologized to staff during his first all‑hands meeting since returning to Nvidia, according to Bloomberg, The New York Times, and The Handbasket’s Marisa Kabas. He said he was trying to distance himself from a narrative that the White House and tech leaders had helped him regain his position.

During the meeting, Huang reportedly called claims that President Donald Trump was directly involved in his reinstatement—an idea publicly promoted by Trump himself—“completely untrue.” He added, “Don’t think for a second politics played a role in the company. We are the most apolitical company,” according to Kabas.
summary: Jensen Huang apologized to Nvidia staff during his first all‑hands meeting since returning to the company. He said claims that President Donald Trump directly helped his reinstatement are “completely untrue” and asserted the company is apolitical.
author: The Verge

title: TikTok outage on Tuesday disrupts videos and search, resolves by late afternoon
content:
TikTok experienced a service disruption earlier on Tuesday, with videos, search results, favorites and other features failing to load as usual. The outage affected the For You feed on iPhone, search results on iOS, Android and the web, profile pages that displayed blank screens, and video links that did not work.

By about 3:45 PM ET the platform appeared to be functioning normally again. Downdetector recorded roughly 25,000 user reports of the issue at around 2:56 PM ET, adding to a series of outages reported over the past couple of weeks.
summary: TikTok experienced an outage on Tuesday that prevented videos, search results, favorites and other features from loading on iOS, Android and the web. The problem appeared to be resolved by about 3:45 PM ET after roughly 25,000 reports were logged on Downdetector.
author: The Verge

title: Take-Two issues DMCA takedown, shuts down Leonida GTA VI PC project
content:
Take‑Two Interactive issued a DMCA takedown notice today that forced the removal of “Leonida,” a fan‑run recompilation project for Grand Theft Auto VI. The effort, created by 15‑year‑old “NotRexed,” was intended to translate a leaked Xbox version of GTA VI so it could run natively on Windows.

The leak, posted earlier this week by leaker “Cyberleek,” included a full Xbox build of the game and several gameplay videos released over the summer. Following the leak, modders have accelerated attempts to reverse‑engineer the code and rebuild it for PC, but the Leonida project has now been shut down.
summary: Take-Two sent a DMCA takedown notice that caused the Leonida fan project, created by 15‑year‑old “NotRexed,” to disappear. Leonida was intended to translate a leaked GTA VI Xbox build to run natively on Windows.
author: The Verge

title: US Army to Detonate 9,700 Pounds of Lead Azide at Iowa Ammunition Plant
content:
The U.S. Army is proceeding with a planned detonation of its lead azide stockpile at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa. The explosion is scheduled for approximately 9:00 AM Central Standard Time on Wednesday. A sign identifying the facility is visible inside the fence surrounding the plant, as captured in a Getty Images photo on November 19.

The material to be detonated consists of 68 drums containing roughly 9,700 pounds of lead azide, an unstable chemical compound used to initiate munitions such as grenades. Lead azide has been employed by the U.S. military as a primary explosive for nearly a century. About fifteen years ago, the Army began moving away from the compound because of the challenges associated with storing and transporting it, according to expert Robert Cekada.
summary: The US Army plans to detonate about 9,700 pounds of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa. The detonation is scheduled for 9:00 AM CST on Wednesday.
author: The Verge

title: FinCEN Investigates Cybersecurity Incident with Unauthorized System Access
content:
The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), a bureau within the Treasury Department, announced on Tuesday that it is investigating a “cybersecurity incident” that led to unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems. FinCEN did not disclose the full scope or source of the breach but said it has taken some systems offline as a precautionary measure.

The disclosure follows a report by The New York Times that the Central Intelligence Agency and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence had identified a breach of an open‑source intelligence system, exposing unclassified information.
summary: FinCEN, part of the Treasury Department, disclosed it is investigating a cybersecurity incident that caused unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems. The bureau has taken some systems offline as a precaution and has not released details on the scope or source of the breach.
author: The Verge

title: Kalshi pauses Utah trading after losing court battles
content:
Kalshi announced that it is pausing its operations in Utah after a series of court defeats, spokesperson Jacki McGavick said Monday. The company lost a legal effort to block Utah’s ongoing enforcement actions under the state’s gambling statutes.

The decision comes as multiple lawsuits in Utah continue to proceed, and Kalshi’s request to a federal appeals court to stay those cases pending an appeal was rejected. An emergency motion filed by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, which maintains that it has exclusive jurisdiction over prediction‑market trading, also did not prevent Utah’s enforcement actions, and a federal district court has not granted that motion.
summary: Kalshi made the “difficult decision” to pause operations in Utah after losing a court fight to block the state’s ongoing enforcement actions under Utah gambling laws, Kalshi spokesperson Jacki McGavick said Monday. It seems Kalshi’s legal troubles in Utah have become too much for the prediction market platform to gamble on continued operations there.
author: Ars Technica

title: OSU study shows timing and amount of smoke‑tainted hops key to beer quality
content:
Oregon State University scientists have investigated how brewers can mitigate the effects of smoke‑tainted hops that resulted from the 2020 wildfires, which burned over one million acres, destroyed thousands of structures, and killed 11 people. Smoke from the fires spread across the region and adversely affected hops grown for beer brewing, a crop that supplies more than 95 percent of U.S. hops and about 40 percent of the global supply.

In a new paper published in the Journal of the American Society of Brewing Chemists, the researchers found that the impact of smoke‑tainted hops depends on both the quantity of affected hops used and the timing of their addition during the brewing process. The study suggests that brewers can still incorporate these hops while reducing negative flavor contributions.

Thomas Shellhammer, an OSU chemist who co‑authored the paper, previously identified the growing popularity of dry hopping—adding hops after fermentation, common for pale ales—as a likely cause of the exploding beer bottle phenomenon.
summary: OSU scientists found that the protection of beers from smoke‑tainted hops depends on the amount of affected hops used and when they are added during brewing. The findings were published in the Journal of the American Society of Brewing Chemists and co‑authored by OSU chemist Thomas Shellhammer.
author: Ars Technica

title: Amazon Leo adds 36 satellites via Ariane 6 after Vulcan failure, speeds up Falcon 9 launches
content:
Amazon’s Leo broadband constellation has received a significant boost after a European Ariane 6 launch carried 36 satellites into orbit on Tuesday. The launch followed the loss of 40 satellites earlier this month when United Launch Alliance’s Vulcan rocket failed, leaving Amazon’s primary launch provider grounded. With the Ariane 6 flight, the Amazon Leo fleet now totals 432 satellites, a key step in filling the gap left by the Vulcan outage.

In a statement to Ars, an Amazon official announced that the company is accelerating several Falcon 9 launches it has purchased from SpaceX. SpaceX also operates the Starlink satellite network, which Amazon aims to surpass. The next Falcon 9 launch for Amazon Leo is now scheduled for December, a date moved forward from the previous plan for next year.

Following the December flight, Amazon has several additional Falcon 9 missions planned to deploy Leo satellites in rapid succession, further expanding the constellation’s coverage.
summary: A European Ariane 6 launch placed 36 satellites into orbit for Amazon's Leo broadband constellation, bringing the fleet to 432 satellites after 40 were lost in a United Launch Alliance Vulcan failure. Amazon said it is accelerating Falcon 9 launches, moving the next flight to December and scheduling additional Falcon 9 missions in rapid succession.
author: Ars Technica

title: Amazon drone crashes onto Michigan garage after delivering shampoo, FAA investigates
content: An Amazon delivery drone that clipped a fiber-optic line before crashing onto a garage roof is now the subject of an investigation by the US Federal Aviation Administration. It’s the latest delivery drone mishap caught on video as Amazon and other companies are ramping up such aerial delivery operations across the United States. The November 20 incident began with Jim Brennan and his wife, residents of Huntington Woods, Michigan, placing an order for shampoo and being surprised by a notification about the package arriving by drone within seven minutes, according to WXYZ 7 News Detroit. After the drone dropped the package into Brennan’s backyard, it lost a propeller when it caught on fiber-optic cable and floundered sideways before getting pinned between the neighbor’s garage roof and some power lines. “Like a sick bird, it tried to go up, it tried to get out of here,” Brennan told WXYZ 7. Read full article Comments
summary: On November 20, an Amazon delivery drone clipped a fiber‑optic line and crashed onto a garage roof in Huntington Woods, Michigan after dropping a shampoo package for Jim Brennan and his wife. The crash, which left the drone pinned between the garage and power lines, is now being investigated by the US Federal Aviation Administration.
author: Ars Technica

title: Mathematician uses AI to produce proof of Riemann hypothesis
content:
Last week a report emerged that a mathematician employed artificial‑intelligence tools to produce a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, one of mathematics’ most celebrated open problems. The announcement follows a series of recent breakthroughs in the discipline that have been either facilitated by or wholly generated with large‑language‑model systems, a development that has unsettled many researchers in the field.

The Riemann hypothesis, first formulated by Bernhard Riemann in the mid‑1800s, concerns the distribution of prime numbers and underpins work in number theory and cryptography. Wikipedia describes it as “one of the most important problems in the field” of pure mathematics. While the proof itself has not yet been examined in detail, mathematicians are currently reviewing the claim and assessing its implications for the broader mathematical community.
summary: A mathematician announced a proof of the Riemann hypothesis that was aided by artificial intelligence. Researchers are currently examining the proof and its implications.
author: Ars Technica

title: Microsoft declares “Code Red” overhaul after historic November 12 cloud outage
content:
Microsoft has launched a “Code Red” overhaul of its engineering response practices after a November 12 outage that blocked access to Exchange Online, Teams and Outlook for users worldwide. Internal memos reviewed by Reuters show Microsoft 365 Core President Jason Henderson calling the incident the greatest customer impact in Exchange Online’s history. Henderson also noted that an urgent production fix in a recent incident required five to six days to achieve worldwide saturation, while the company’s goal for its most urgent security fixes is to move from detection to safe worldwide deployment within one hour—a target it has not yet met.

A post‑incident report dated November 20 attributes the downtime to an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July, which created lock contention in gateway processes. A Teams traffic failover then added extra load to infrastructure already strained, because maintenance had left roughly 14 percent of gateway server capacity offline at the time of the incident. The memos outlining these findings have not been published by Microsoft.
summary: Microsoft declares “Code Red” overhaul after historic November 12 cloud outage.
author: Ars Technica

title: NASA suspends science on Perseverance rover and Odyssey orbiter due to technical issues
content:
Two of NASA’s four active Mars missions have temporarily halted science operations after encountering separate technical problems. The affected spacecraft are the Perseverance rover and the Odyssey orbiter, both of which are operating beyond their original design lifetimes.

Perseverance, now in its sixth year on the Martian surface, has been gathering rock and soil samples for a future return to Earth and is currently studying the rim of a crater that once held an ancient lake. The rover’s outage is linked to its communications system, which includes two redundant UHF radios for high‑rate links to orbiters and a separate X‑band antenna for lower‑rate direct‑to‑Earth transmissions.

Odyssey, launched in 2001 and the longest‑living Mars mission, is also offline for science work while its technical issue is addressed. Both suspensions are described as hopefully temporary.
summary: Two of NASA's four Mars missions, the Perseverance rover and the Odyssey orbiter, have suspended science operations because of separate technical issues. Both spacecraft are operating beyond their original design lifetimes, with Perseverance in its sixth year studying a crater rim and Odyssey, launched in 2001, being the longest-lived Mars mission.
author: Ars Technica

title: New benchmark shows top AI agents struggle with everyday tasks
content: A new benchmark shows that, despite widespread use of personal AI assistants, even the most advanced AI models have difficulty completing everyday tasks reliably and safely, and may introduce new problems. The findings highlight ongoing limitations in current AI agents’ everyday performance.
summary: Millions are adopting personal AI assistants. A new benchmark reveals that even the most advanced AI models fail to complete everyday tasks reliably and safely without creating potential new problems.
author: TechCrunch

title: Trump says pardoning Nvidia co‑founder Jensen Huang is an option
content: The New York Post says that, in an exclusive interview, the President said that pardoning the Nvidia co-founder is "an option," but not one that he thought he would need to use.
summary: Trump says pardoning Nvidia co‑founder Jensen Huang is an option.
author: TechCrunch

title: Yale's Jeffrey Sonnenfeld warns Nvidia harms U.S. industrial might
content: Yale professor Jeffrey Sonnenfeld cautioned that the market’s enthusiasm on Monday for Jensen Huang’s White House‑backed return as Nvidia’s chief executive and board member may be a serious error. Sonnenfeld said the move could expose Nvidia’s directors to “historic” personal liability amid an expanding slate of lawsuits. He also questioned whether the United States should celebrate a company that, in his view, has contributed advanced chips to adversary nations, suggesting Nvidia may be a detriment rather than a champion of U.S. industrial strength.
summary: Sonnenfeld cautioned that Jensen Huang's White House‑backed return as Nvidia CEO and board member could be a major mistake. He said the move may expose directors to historic personal liability and questioned celebrating a company that supplies advanced chips to adversaries.
author: TechCrunch

title: Tech stocks retreat as Nvidia falls 6% after Jensen Huang's return
content:
Technology shares led a market retreat on Tuesday, as investors braced for further volatility in the AI sector that drives global economic growth. The sell‑off followed a return of Jensen Huang to the CEO position at Nvidia, days after he had been forced to resign.  

A day after Huang’s reinstatement sent Nvidia shares up more than 30% and added over $900 billion to the company’s market value, the euphoria faded. By the close of trading on Tuesday, Nvidia’s stock had fallen almost 6%, marking a sharp reversal of the earlier rally.
summary: Technology shares led a market retreat on Tuesday as investors grew cautious after Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia’s CEO days after his forced resignation. Nvidia’s stock, which had risen more than 30% and added over $900 billion in market value after his return, slipped almost 6% by Tuesday’s close.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Nvidia staff give CEO Jensen Huang standing ovation on return to Santa Clara HQ
content: Nvidia employees cheered and applauded CEO Jensen Huang as he returned to the company's headquarters in Santa Clara, California, on Monday, 11 days after stepping down.
summary: Nvidia employees gave CEO Jensen Huang a standing ovation as he returned to the company's headquarters in Santa Clara, California. The ovation took place on Monday, 11 days after he stepped down.
author: Euronews

title: Israeli strikes kill Hamas security chief, six others in Gaza
content:
Israeli forces struck a police station in southern Gaza, resulting in the deaths of two policemen.  

In Israel, ongoing coalition talks have left caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in charge of military operations.
summary: Israeli strikes in Gaza killed Hamas security chief and six other people. The attacks also hit a police station in southern Gaza, killing two policemen, while caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu remains in charge of military operations during coalition talks.
author: Euronews

title: US and Armenia start building Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity
content: The United States and Armenia have launched the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP), a regional transit initiative that has entered construction. The project follows a Washington summit that brokered peace between Armenia and Azerbaijan, and Baku has welcomed the development amid broader geopolitical reshaping.
summary: The United States and Armenia have launched the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP) project, which has entered its construction phase. The launch comes a year after the Washington summit that brought peace between Armenia and Azerbaijan.
author: Euronews

title: Istanbul lioness sighting prompts search, authorities say no big cat found
content: Reports of a lioness roaming north of Istanbul triggered a security scramble after grainy footage appeared to show a large cat prowling across open land. After a day of searches, Turkish authorities confirmed that the animal was neither a lion nor any other big cat.
summary: Grainy footage that appeared to show a lioness roaming north of Istanbul led Turkish authorities to launch a large search. After a day of searching, officials said the animal was not a lion or any other big cat.
author: Euronews

title: Sixteen chefs vie for world egg mayonnaise champion title in Saint-Ouen
content: Sixteen finalists gathered near Paris to vie for the world egg mayonnaise championship, held in Saint‑Ouen just outside the city on Monday, 23 November 2026. The event celebrates a deceptively simple French bistro classic that demands considerable culinary skill.
summary: Sixteen finalists gathered near Paris to compete for the title of world egg mayonnaise champion in Saint-Ouen on Monday 23 November 2026. The competition celebrates a deceptively simple French bistro classic that demands considerable culinary skill.
author: Euronews

title: Rosstat leak shows at least 490,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine
content: A data leak from Russia’s statistics agency, Rosstat, shows that at least 490,000 Russian soldiers have died in Ukraine. The figure was extracted by two hacking groups on 1 November from death certificates recorded up to the end of August, excluding missing servicemen and deaths not yet documented.
summary: Two hacking groups extracted the data from Rosstat on 1 November. The figure, based on death certificates registered through August, shows at least 490,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine and excludes missing servicemen and deaths not yet recorded.
author: Euronews

title: Car bomb in central Colombia injures at least 24; President de la Espriella visits site
content: A car bomb detonated in central Colombia, leaving at least 24 people injured. Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella arrived in Villavicencio at about 9 a.m. local time on Tuesday to hold a security meeting and visit the blast site.
summary: Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella arrived in Villavicencio at around 9 am local time on Tuesday as he prepared to hold a security meeting and visit the scene of the blast.
author: Euronews

title: Nvidia Allegations: Trump Administration Favorable Treatment and Pay‑to‑Play Claims
content:
François Picard welcomed Andrew Weissmann, a Professor of Practice at NYU School of Law and former federal prosecutor noted for leading major DOJ and FBI investigations. Picard asked, “Why were they treating Nvidia so favorably?” to set the tone for the discussion.  

Weissmann will examine the legal and ethical questions surrounding the Trump administration’s dealings with the chipmaker. He will address allegations of personal financial gain, the implications for U.S. national security, the limits of presidential immunity, and what he calls an “unholy alliance of tech bros, of Wall Street, and of politicians.”
summary: Nvidia Allegations: Trump Administration Favorable Treatment and Pay‑to‑Play Claims.
author: France 24

title: Jensen Huang's Nvidia comeback sends AI videos into overdrive
content: Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia as CEO 11 days after his resignation, prompting a surge of AI‑generated videos that reference his comeback. The online response shifted from last week’s memes that mocked him to a wave of celebratory content. A viral clip that appeared to show Huang dancing was identified as AI‑manipulated footage of a basketball coach from 2016. According to Vedika Bahl, the AI technology Nvidia helped popularise is now reshaping the narrative surrounding its chief executive.
summary: Just 11 days after resigning as Nvidia CEO, Jensen Huang’s return has unleashed a fresh wave of AI-generated videos. But the internet has changed its tune: while last week’s memes mocked Huang, many now celebrate his comeback.
author: France 24

title: Trump reinstates Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, prompting congressional and judicial scrutiny
content:
Angela Diffley welcomed Bernard Benhamou, Secretary General of the Institute of Digital Sovereignty and Senior Lecturer in Internet Governance at Paris 1 Panthéon‑Sorbonne University.  

Benhamou discussed Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia, asking what it means for Trump, Lutnick, the US, the AI industry and China. He called Huang “the global banker of the AI industry” and said, “He is the visionary, he is the banker. He's not only the chip maker.”  

Benhamou warned that Donald Trump’s decision to reinstate the Nvidia CEO could bring congressional and judicial scrutiny. He added, “It’s far from over. It’s just the beginning.”
summary: Angela Diffley welcomed Bernard Benhamou, Secretary General of the Institute of Digital Sovereignty and Senior Lecturer in Internet Governance at Paris 1 Panthéon‑Sorbonne University. Benhamou warned that Donald Trump’s decision to reinstate Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang could bring congressional and judicial scrutiny.
author: France 24

title: Nvidia shares fall as Jensen Huang reinstated amid tech executives' Trump investment
content: Nvidia shares fell on Tuesday as the historic rally sparked by Jensen Huang's return as CEO quickly lost steam, with investors refocusing ​on the political ‌and governance risks surrounding his reinstatement. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney, The Hill Senior Technology Reporter Miranda Nazzaro says that the reinstatement of Jensen Huang at Nvidia represents "the culmination of a two-year push of tech executives to get closer to President Trump and their investment in the President is clearly paying off".
summary: Nvidia shares fall as Jensen Huang reinstated amid tech executives' Trump investment.
author: France 24

title: Real Madrid thrash PSV 5-1 in comeback as Manchester City draws 2-2 with Napoli
content:
Real Madrid extended their winning streak to ten matches across all competitions on Tuesday, overturning an early goal to defeat PSV Eindhoven 5‑1 in the Champions League. Jude Bellingham scored a spectacular goal, and Kylian Mbappé added two goals as part of the rout.

In the same round of fixtures, Manchester City recovered from two deficits to finish 2‑2 with Napoli, while Arsenal were held to a 1‑1 draw by Borussia Dortmund.
summary: Real Madrid thrash PSV 5-1 in comeback as Manchester City draws 2-2 with Napoli.
author: France 24

title: New York Jury Convicts Huawei of Stealing Trade Secrets, Acquits on Other Charges
content: A New York jury found Chinese telecom company Huawei guilty of stealing trade secrets and other criminal offenses, while acquitting the firm of a racketeering conspiracy and obstruction of justice. The verdict concluded a three‑month trial in New York and adds to ongoing U.S. actions aimed at limiting Huawei’s operations amid alleged national‑security concerns.
summary: A New York jury found Chinese telecom giant Huawei guilty of stealing trade secrets and other criminal offences. The jury acquitted Huawei of racketeering conspiracy and obstruction of justice after a three-month trial.
author: France 24

title: Ukraine asks for €115 billion foreign aid for 2027, says President Zelensky
content: President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine will need €115 billion in external financing next year to sustain its economy and war effort against Russia. He noted that Kyiv has already secured commitments for roughly €90 billion from the European Union.
summary: Ukraine will need €115 billion in external financing next year to sustain its economy and war effort against Russia, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Tuesday. He added that Kyiv had secured commitments for about €90 billion from the European Union.
author: France 24

title: Zelenskyy urges swift NATO membership as Berlin assembly shows no unanimity
content: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is urging a swift acceptance of Ukraine into NATO, but unanimity among member states is absent, as demonstrated at the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin. The country’s bid for membership and calls for additional air‑defence capabilities are described as controversial.
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is calling for the rapid acceptance of Ukraine into NATO. The NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin demonstrated that the required unanimity for membership is lacking.
author: DW World

title: Irish EU presidency offers UK partner status for car assembly, boosting Burnham's EU reset
content: Irish presidency of EU proposes giving UK ‘partner’ status on assembly of cars in possible boost to reset of relations The UK would not have to follow the EU and apply tariffs on Chinese car imports under an Irish proposal that could prove another breakthrough for the prime minister, Andy Burnham, in his reset of relations with the bloc. The proposal comes as the UK’s foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, told a parliamentary committee that there had been “a transformation in the EU view”.
summary: Irish EU presidency offers UK partner status for car assembly, boosting Burnham's EU reset.
author: Guardian World

title: Jury begins deliberations in Beau Lamarre-Condon double murder trial
content:
After a ten‑week trial, a 12‑person jury has begun deliberations in the double‑murder case against former police officer Beau Lamarre‑Condon. The jurors will decide whether Lamar‑Condon is responsible for the deaths of Jesse Baird and his new partner, Luke Davies.

Prosecutors allege that Lamar‑Condon used his police service weapon to fatally shoot Baird and Davies inside Baird’s home in Paddington on 19 February 2024. The verdict now rests with the jury.
summary: After a 10‑week trial, a 12‑person jury has been sent to deliberate in the double‑murder case against former police officer Beau Lamarre‑Condon. He is accused of fatally shooting Jesse Baird and Luke Davies with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024.
author: Guardian World

title: Australia inflation rises to 4.9% in year to October, up from 4.3%
content:
Inflation in Australia rose to 4.9 % in the year to October, up from 4.3 % in September. The increase brings the rate nearly double the Reserve Bank of Australia’s official target of 2.5 %.

The rise is driven by surging fuel costs, which jumped 6.3 % last month, and the removal of electricity rebates. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, electricity prices were 25 % higher than a year earlier, adding to cost‑of‑living pressures that peak ahead of Christmas.
summary: Australia inflation rises to 4.9% in year to October, up from 4.3%.
author: Guardian World

title: Former officer Beau Lamarre-Condon guilty of murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies
content: A New South Wales Supreme Court jury delivered its verdict on Wednesday, finding former police officer Beau Lamarre‑Condon guilty of two counts of murder. The jury concluded that Lamarre‑Condon killed Jesse Baird and Luke Davies with his service weapon in Baird’s Sydney home. The verdict was reached after two hours of deliberation.
summary: A New South Wales supreme court jury found former police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon guilty of two counts of murder. He was convicted of killing Jesse Baird and Luke Davies with his service weapon in Baird’s Sydney home after two hours of deliberation.
author: Guardian World

title: Marles apologises to LGBTQ+ veterans as Australia signs treaty with Solomon Islands
content: Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast Wells says AI investment and creative protections not a ‘zero-sum game’ Weighing into the gigantic debate that is AI companies wanting to scrape Australian data to train models versus creatives who want to protect their work, Anika Wells says it’s not a ‘zero-sum’ game. I reject this sort of zero-sum game where building Australian sovereignty in AI must come at the expense of creatives or at diminishing the rights of creatives. At the moment, yes, we want deals, but we want creatives paid properly for their work. And the situation that we find ourselves in at the moment is that they’re not. They have no control and often no payment for their work.
summary: Marles apologised to LGBTQ+ veterans. Australia and the Solomon Islands signed a historic treaty.
author: Guardian World

title: Cuba's life expectancy drops to 74.4 years, first decline since 1950
content:
The World Health Organization’s chief, Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, announced that Cuba’s life expectancy has fallen for the first time since records began in 1950. He cited a drop from 78.8 years in 2020 to 74.4 years in 2025, based on figures that predate the U.S. fuel blockade.

Ghebreyesus made the statement during a visit to Havana, noting that the decline occurs amid a severe economic crisis affecting the island. The announcement marks a historic reversal in Cuba’s long‑standing trend of rising life expectancy.
summary: Cuba's life expectancy drops to 74.4 years, first decline since 1950.
author: Guardian World

title: Armed men hold hostages in Cartagena supermarket, 15 released
content: President says 15 people released and Cartagena incident stems from botched robbery by ‘common criminals’ Armed and masked men have been holding people hostage in a supermarket since early Tuesday morning in Cartagena, one of Colombia’s most popular tourist cities. The country’s president, Abelardo de la Espriella, said 30 people had initially been taken hostage, but five had been released, and hours later local media reported that another 10 had also been freed.
summary: Armed, masked men have been holding people hostage in a supermarket in Cartagena since early Tuesday morning. President Abelardo de la Espriella said 30 were taken hostage and that 15 have been released.
author: Guardian World

title: Kilmar Ábrego García to depart US for Spain after deportation case
content: Salvadorian citizen Kilmar Ábrego García, who was deported in March 2025 and later returned to the United States after a Supreme Court ruling, is departing the country voluntarily. His lawyers confirmed on Tuesday that Ábrego will leave for Spain on Tuesday evening.
summary: Salvadorian man Kilmar Ábrego García, who was deported in March 2025 and returned to the United States after a Supreme Court ruling, is leaving the country of his own volition. His lawyers confirmed he will travel to Spain on Tuesday evening.
author: Guardian World

title: China launching 1st international astronaut to Tiangong space station today: Watch it live
content:
China is set to launch its first international astronaut to the Tiangong space station on November 24, marking a historic milestone for the nation’s space program. The Shenzhou-24 mission will lift off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China at 7:18 p.m. EST (8:18 a.m. Beijing time on November 25) aboard a Long March 2F rocket. This flight represents China’s 18th crewed spaceflight and its 12th mission to the three-module Tiangong station, which was completed in low Earth orbit in late 2022.

The crew includes commander Tang Hongbo, flight engineer Wu Yi, and payload specialist Muhammad Zeeshan Ali. Ali, a former pilot in Pakistan’s armed forces, will be the first person from his country to reach orbit. His selection followed a spaceflight cooperation agreement signed between China and Pakistan in February 2025, after which two Pakistani candidates traveled to China for training. China announced the final crew on November 23, consistent with its practice of revealing astronaut identities only the day before launch.

Tang Hongbo, who previously flew on the Shenzhou-12 and Shenzhou-17 missions, will become the first person to visit Tiangong three times. Wu Yi is embarking on her first spaceflight. While Tang and Wu are expected to remain aboard the station for the standard six-month rotation, Ali will stay in orbit for approximately one week. He will return to Earth with Zhang Zhiyuan and Lai Ka-ying of the Shenzhou-23 mission, which launched on May 24.

The Shenzhou-23 crewmate Zhu Yangzhu will remain on Tiangong after Ali’s departure, staying until the Shenzhou-24 crew returns. This arrangement will make Zhu the first Chinese astronaut to spend a year in orbit, a milestone intended to prepare China for future long-duration missions to the moon and other deep-space destinations.
summary: China will send an international astronaut to its Tiangong space station today (Nov. 24) for the first time ever, and you can watch the landmark liftoff live.

title: YunLone Galaxy Projector review: $28 star light offers app control and aurora effects
content:
The YunLone Galaxy Projector is a star projector priced at approximately $28, designed to display aurora-style light patterns on walls and ceilings. The device measures 3.54 by 3.15 by 4.72 inches and weighs 17.6 ounces. It features an LED bulb, a laser, a built-in speaker, and a sleep timer. Operation is supported by both a companion app and a remote control, and the unit includes rotation capabilities. The manufacturer describes the product as a customizable night light intended for creating a relaxing atmosphere in living rooms or bedrooms.

The design of the YunLone Galaxy Projector prioritizes functionality over aesthetics. It has a circular shape with a clear globe in the center that serves as the projector. The unit sits on rubberized feet to prevent slipping and is naturally tilted to point slightly diagonally, which helps spread the lights across the room. The build quality is described as sturdy, made from hard-wearing plastic that is suitable for use in a child’s bedroom. The front of the unit has limited buttons, and the overall appearance is basic rather than decorative.

In terms of performance, the projector displays colorful, dancing auroras rather than accurate scientific constellations or close-ups of the moon. Users can control the projection via an app for Android or Apple smartphones, allowing for extensive customization. The app offers preset arrangements labeled by seasons, colors, or holidays, as well as a color wheel for creating custom schemes. Users can also adjust brightness, enable a "breathing" effect, and control the speed of the ripples. A laser feature projects green stars, which can be turned off independently or adjusted for brightness. The projection has a wide reach, covering most of the walls and ceiling in the test bedroom.

Functionality includes a Bluetooth speaker with decent audio quality, suitable for audiobooks and podcasts, though it lacks significant bass. The device also contains eight built-in sound effects, such as white noise, waves, lullabies, and a storm. While the app provides superior control, the bundled remote control, which requires two AAA batteries, offers more limited options for setting basic colors and speeds. The pairing process with the app is noted as not being entirely straightforward, requiring the user to quickly turn the unit on and off three times to enter pairing mode, which may take several attempts.

The review concludes that the YunLone Galaxy Projector is a strong option for those seeking a budget-friendly, non-scientific projector for relaxation. For users interested in accurate astronomical projections, the review suggests alternatives such as the Sega Toys Homestar Classic or the Hommkiety Galaxy Projector. The Sega Toys range offers excellent projections but comes with a higher price tag and requires purchasing extra discs for different images. The Hommkiety Galaxy Projector, priced closer to $50, includes several interchangeable discs in the box for displaying various space images.
summary: The YunLone Galaxy Projector costs around $28 and features a laser, Bluetooth speaker, and app support for extensive color customization. Reviewers describe it as a sturdy, functional unit that projects wide-reaching aurora patterns, though it does not display accurate scientific constellations.

title: Joe Biden memoir defends decisions, blames party for re-election loss
content: New memoir tells of policy feats and battles with Trump but struggles to take responsibility for re-election debacle Inevitably, readers of Joe Biden’s new memoir will flick forward to find what he says about the events that ended his presidency: increasing pressure about his age and capacity that finally led him to stand aside and anoint Kamala Harris, too late, ushering fascism back to the White House. Alas, Biden thinks he was just fine to keep on serving and the whole thing was a stitch-up by a panicked party. Of his catastrophic debate in June 2024, when the then 81-year-old president blinked, stuttered and gaped under the lights, Biden writes: “I knew the debate had gone badly. But I knew that debates had gone badly for lots of incumbent presidents. Especially their first ones. I left the stage thinking I would be debating Trump once more before the election was over. I was wrong. This wasn’t just the first debate, it was my last one.” He raises Barack Obama’s poor performance in his first debate with Mitt Romney in 2012, when Biden was VP. Caught cold, Obama prepared for the next one and cruised to re-election.
summary: Joe Biden’s new memoir details his policy achievements and conflicts with Trump while arguing that his withdrawal from the presidential race was forced by a panicked party. The book defends his performance in the June 2024 debate by comparing it to Barack Obama’s poor first debate in 2012.

title: From Sovereigns to Servants by Alexandra Prokopenko review – Putin and his yes men
content: A disturbing account of the way Russia’s elites have reduced themselves to craven courtiers When Vladimir Putin launched his full-scale invasion of Ukraine four and a half years ago, it was a shock, but it wasn’t a surprise. The US and the UK had been publicly warning their allies for weeks about what Russia was planning, as well as threatening the Russians with a wave of sanctions unprecedented against a major power. Putin’s foreign policy had long relied on confusion and untruth. By saying that they knew exactly what he was up to, Britain and America were hoping first to deny him his usual ambiguity, and second to pressure the men around him into making him stop, since war would deprive them of the stolen assets they’d stashed in London’s most exclusive neighbourhoods.
summary: The review describes Alexandra Prokopenko’s book as a disturbing account of Russia’s elites reducing themselves to craven courtiers. It notes that Putin’s full‑scale invasion of Ukraine began four and a half years ago and that the US and UK warned allies and threatened unprecedented sanctions to pressure those around him.

title: Only 3.8% of GTA VI reviewers were women despite female protagonist
content:
Grand Theft Auto VI has emerged as the biggest video game launch of all time, breaking sales and streaming records to become the best-reviewed game ever, surpassing 1998’s The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. The release is described as a once-in-a-lifetime phenomenon that will shape the gaming medium and pop culture for years, occurring while developers at studio Rockstar Games fight for their rights. Notably, this is the first Grand Theft Auto title in thirty years to feature a female protagonist, who is also a woman of colour.

Despite the game’s cultural significance and its historic lead character, very few women reviewed the title before its release. When the review embargo lifted on 18 November, a stark gender imbalance was evident among the 156 reviewers, with only six appearing to be women. This represents just 3.8% of the total, a statistic highlighted by journalist Lex Luddy in a BlueSky post. The source notes that seemingly no women of colour participated in the pre-release reviews, creating a contrast between the game’s inclusive protagonist and the demographic of its critical reception.
summary: Grand Theft Auto VI became the best-reviewed game ever and the biggest video game launch of all time. Despite featuring the first female protagonist in the series, only six of 156 pre-release reviewers appeared to be women.

title: GTA VI becomes largest video game release with 364.5m streaming hours
content:
Grand Theft Auto VI recently became the largest video game release of all time, with current estimates indicating that at least 30 million people are playing the title. The game’s launch has generated significant engagement from content creators, who have produced hundreds of millions of hours of video content since its release.

According to streaming data from analytics company Streams Charts, a cumulative 364.5 million hours of the game were watched within just two days of its launch. This volume of viewing time is equivalent to roughly 41,000 years of content. The data highlights the massive scale of audience interest in Rockstar Game’s long-awaited title, translating the total watch time into activities such as rifling through cash registers, hanging drywall, birding, diving, or hijacking jets.
summary: Grand Theft Auto VI became the largest video game release of all time, with current estimates indicating at least 30 million players. Streaming data from Streams Charts shows a cumulative 364.5 million hours were watched within two days of its release.

The original final, played in January, saw Senegal beat Morocco 1‑0 after the Moroccan side walked off the pitch. The CAF‑appointed appeals panel later overturned the result, awarding Morocco a 3‑0 win, before CAS reversed the decision.

title: COP31 collapses as fossil fuel producers stall progress
content:
Bill McGuire argues that the recent collapse of the Cop31 climate summit represents a failure of leadership despite a year marked by deadly floods and fires. He asserts that fossil fuel producers are obstructing progress, causing the global community to face the consequences of inaction. McGuire contends that humanity is not sleepwalking into climate catastrophe but is instead moving toward it with full awareness, knowingly jeopardizing the lives of future generations.

The article outlines severe projected climate impacts, stating that UK summer temperatures could reach the mid-40s Celsius within decades, leading to extreme drought, harvest failures, and overheated homes. It notes that Europe, identified as the fastest-heating continent, may break the 50C temperature mark as early as next year. Furthermore, the text claims that by 2050, humid heatwaves in parts of China, South Asia, and the Gulf region could kill thousands of people in a single day.

McGuire highlights that carbon dioxide emissions continue at a rate equivalent to 800,000 Titanics annually, with no visible end. He criticizes the latest climate summit for collapsing in disarray, noting its inability to agree on even a vague statement regarding the transition away from fossil fuels. This failure is framed as a significant setback for the only global initiative capable of reversing the current trajectory.
summary: Fossil fuel producers are stalling progress on climate action, while the COP31 meeting collapsed in disarray. The conference failed to agree on any wording about transitioning away from fossil fuels.

title: Campaigners urge Albanese to reject NSW coal expansion after Cop31

Advocates argue that the government should heed a “line in the sand” warning regarding fossil fuels, which was issued by dozens of countries during the Cop31 UN climate summit.

The source notes that a proposed agreement at the Cop31 negotiations in Turkey failed because a group of nations—including European Union members, Panama, the Marshall Islands, Vanuatu, Norway, and Belize—refused to support it. These nations stated they would not back the agreement unless it contained an explicit statement that the world must transition away from fossil fuels.
summary: Climate campaigners are urging the Albanese government to refuse a coalmine expansion in New South Wales that would allow 430 million tonnes of additional coal extraction. This follows a failed Cop31 agreement where nations demanded an explicit statement on transitioning away from fossil fuels.
